checklist.step: Close the statutory ledger and freeze the trial balance
actions: Confirm with the Senior Accountant that all statutory-basis entries are posted: non-admitted asset write-offs, deferred premium, unearned premium, IMR/AVR (life) and the deferred tax entry under SSAP No. 101.
Close the period in the GL for each writing company by NAIC company code so no further postings can land in the statement period.
Export the statutory trial balance to the close/consolidation tool and lock it with a version stamp of company, period and export timestamp.
Circulate the frozen TB to the Statutory Reporting Manager and the Reserving Actuary as the single source of the blank.
checklist.done: the period is closed per company and a version-stamped statutory trial balance has been issued to the preparers.

checklist.step: Roll the NAIC statement software forward to the current blank year
actions: Install the vendor's current-year annual statement release and confirm it carries the NAIC Blanks (E) Working Group changes adopted for this statement year.
Roll each company forward so prior-year columns populate, and verify the rolled prior-year Assets, Liabilities and Surplus agree to last year's filed blank to the dollar.
Set company demographics on the Jurat: NAIC company code, FEIN, state of domicile, statutory home office address, and the list of states in which the company is licensed.
Read the current-year instruction change summary with the Regulatory Reporting Analyst and list every new or renumbered line, schedule or interrogatory as a preparation task.
checklist.done: the current-year blank is installed, rolled forward tying to the prior filing, with instruction changes converted into named preparation tasks.

checklist.step: Map the frozen trial balance to NAIC blank line numbers
actions: Open the TB-to-blank mapping workbook and refresh it against the current chart of accounts, flagging accounts added since last close.
Assign every account to a blank page and line number (for example Page 2 Line 1 bonds, Page 3 Line 1 losses, Page 4 Line 1 premiums earned) and leave no account unmapped.
Route new or ambiguous accounts to the Controller with the proposed SSAP citation supporting the classification and admitted/non-admitted call.
Import the mapped balances into the statement software and print the import exception report; clear every rejected line before moving on.
checklist.done: every trial balance account maps to a blank line, and the software import exception report is clear.

checklist.step: Build the Assets and Liabilities pages
actions: Complete Page 2 Assets in three columns — gross assets, non-admitted, net admitted — and support each non-admitted amount with the SSAP paragraph that makes it non-admitted (furniture, EDP over the cap, agents' balances over 90 days).

Complete Page 3 Liabilities, Surplus and Other Funds, pulling loss and loss adjustment expense reserves from the Reserving Actuary's signed reserve memo and unearned premium from the policy administration extract.
Confirm total admitted assets on Page 2 equals total liabilities plus capital and surplus on Page 3 with no plug line.
Have the Controller initial the non-admitted asset schedule before the page is locked.
checklist.done: Pages 2 and 3 balance, every non-admitted amount carries an SSAP citation, and the Controller has initialled the non-admitted schedule.

checklist.step: Build the Statement of Income and the Capital and Surplus Account
actions: Complete Page 4 with premiums earned, losses incurred, LAE, other underwriting expenses, net investment income earned and realized capital gains from the investment accounting feed.

Complete the Capital and Surplus Account roll-forward: prior-year surplus, net income, change in net unrealized gains, change in non-admitted assets, change in provision for reinsurance, dividends to stockholders and any surplus contributions.
Tie the ending surplus on Page 4 to Page 3 Line 'Surplus as regards policyholders' and investigate any difference before proceeding — never force the roll-forward.
Send the surplus roll-forward to the Chief Financial Officer with a one-page bridge explaining every movement over 2% of surplus.
checklist.done: the income statement and surplus roll-forward foot, tie to Page 3, and the CFO has the surplus movement bridge.

checklist.step: Build the Cash Flow statement and the cash and invested asset ties
actions: Complete Page 5 Cash Flow: premiums collected net of reinsurance, benefit and loss payments, commissions and expenses paid, net investment income, and cost/proceeds of investments acquired and disposed.
Reconcile the ending 'Cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments' line to the Schedule E Part 1 depository balances and to the bank reconciliations for every account.
Obtain the custodian statement from the Investment Operations Manager and confirm the custodian name and agreement date shown in the General Interrogatories match it.
Document any reconciling item over $25,000 with the bank, date and reason on the cash tie workpaper.
checklist.done: Page 5 ties to Schedule E Part 1 and to the bank reconciliations, with every material reconciling item explained.

checklist.step: Load actuarial reserves and the loss development exhibits
actions: Export the booked net and gross reserve estimate by accident year and line of business from the reserving system at the statement valuation date.
Hand the Statutory Reporting Manager the reserve exhibit tied to the signed reserve memo, split into case reserves, IBNR and defense and cost containment.

Confirm the reserve amounts loaded into Page 3 and into the loss development exhibits (Schedule P for P&C blanks, Exhibit 5 and Schedule S for life blanks) equal the booked memo figures line for line.
Have the Appointed Actuary confirm the Statement of Actuarial Opinion covers exactly the reserve amounts carried in the blank.
checklist.done: booked reserves in the blank equal the signed reserve memo and are the amounts covered by the Actuarial Opinion.

checklist.step: Load the investment detail behind the invested asset lines
actions: Extract the position-level holdings file at the valuation date with CUSIP, par, book/adjusted carrying value, fair value and acquisition date.
Attach the NAIC designation and SVO/CRP rating for every bond and preferred stock, sourcing designations from the NAIC AVS+/VISION filing exemption data rather than an internal rating.
Load the file into the statement software's Schedule D Parts 1 and 2 and confirm the Schedule D summary totals equal Page 2 bond and stock lines.
Flag positions with no NAIC designation to the Controller — an undesignated security drives the wrong RBC charge and blocks the filing.
checklist.done: position detail loads into Schedule D with designations on every security and the schedule totals equal Page 2.

checklist.step: Build the premium-by-state page for the 51-jurisdiction distribution
actions: Extract direct written premium, direct earned premium, direct losses paid and direct losses incurred by state of risk for the statement year from the policy administration and claims extracts.
Load them into Schedule T and into the Exhibit of Premiums and Losses (State Page) for each of the 51 jurisdictions plus Canada/Other Alien.
Confirm the Schedule T grand total direct written premium equals the Underwriting and Investment Exhibit direct written premium, and reconcile any difference to a named booking.
Confirm each state showing premium appears on the licensed-state list on the Jurat — premium written in an unlicensed state is a finding to raise to the Compliance Officer, not a rounding matter.
checklist.done: state premium totals reconcile to the underwriting exhibit and no premium appears in a jurisdiction the company is not licensed in.

checklist.step: Draft the Notes to Financial Statements against the SSAP disclosure checklist
actions: Work the NAIC Notes to Financial Statements disclosure checklist note by note, marking each applicable or not applicable with the reason.

Draft the required notes with current-year numbers: Note 1 accounting practices and any permitted or prescribed practice with its state approval letter, Note 5 investments, Note 9 income taxes, Note 10 related party transactions, Note 23 reinsurance and Note 25 changes in incurred losses.
Obtain the Tax Manager's signed deferred tax admissibility calculation under SSAP No. 101 for the income tax note.
Have Legal Counsel confirm the contingencies note against the current litigation reserve schedule before it is locked.
checklist.done: every checklist note is marked applicable or not with a reason, and drafted notes are supported by the tax and litigation source schedules.

checklist.step: Complete the General Interrogatories and Five-Year Historical data
actions: Answer Part 1 General Interrogatories: ownership and control changes, custodial agreements, officer and director conflicts, and holding company registration status.
Answer Part 2 line-of-business interrogatories, including the questions on unpaid loss reserve methodology and on premium written in states where not licensed.
Populate the Five-Year Historical page and confirm the four prior-year columns match the previously filed statements without re-keying.

Route every 'Yes' answer that requires an attached explanation to the named owner (Corporate Secretary for control questions, Investment Operations Manager for custodial) and attach their written response.
checklist.done: all interrogatories are answered, prior-year historical columns match filed statements, and every 'Yes' has its required attachment.

checklist.step: Run and clear the NAIC validation edits and cross-checks
actions: Run the statement software's full validation set: Level 1 (hard-stop) edits, Level 2 (explanatory) cross-checks and the page-to-schedule cross-checks.
Fix every Level 1 edit at source in the GL mapping or the source extract — never by typing over the derived line in the blank.
For each remaining Level 2 item, write the explanation the NAIC will see and have the Controller approve the wording.
Print the final validation report to PDF as the cross-check clearance log and file it with the statement working papers.
checklist.done: zero Level 1 edits remain, every Level 2 item has a Controller-approved explanation, and the validation report is filed.

checklist.step: Reconcile the completed blank back to the general ledger and to prior filings
actions: Run the blank-to-TB reconciliation for total admitted assets, total liabilities, surplus and net income; investigate any difference above $10,000.
Compare each Page 2, 3 and 4 line to the prior quarter and the prior year and write a variance explanation for every movement over 10% or $1 million.
Recompute the key analytical ratios the state analyst will run — surplus change, premium-to-surplus, reserve-to-surplus — and prepare the explanation for any ratio outside the IRIS usual range.
Sign the reconciliation and pass the package to the Chief Financial Officer for officer review.
checklist.done: the blank reconciles to the GL within tolerance and every material variance and out-of-range IRIS ratio has a written explanation.

checklist.step: Execute the Jurat page with officer signatures and notarisation
actions: Review the officer certification language on the Jurat and the full statement package including the surplus bridge and variance explanations.

Obtain the signatures the blank requires — president or chief executive, secretary and treasurer or chief financial officer — and have them notarised where the domiciliary state requires a notarised original.
Confirm the Jurat lists the correct NAIC company code, FEIN, state of domicile and the names of the Appointed Actuary and the independent CPA firm.
Return the executed Jurat to the Statutory Reporting Manager for scanning into the filing package.
checklist.done: a signed, notarised Jurat with correct company identifiers is attached to the statement package.

checklist.step: Archive the filed statement package as retained evidence
actions: File the complete package — filed PDF blank, the transmitted data file, TB-to-blank mapping, cross-check clearance log, reserve memo, signed Jurat and the NAIC submission confirmation — under company code and statement period.
Apply the 7-year retention label and lock the folder against edit so the filed version cannot drift from what the NAIC holds.
Register the package location on the compliance evidence index so a California Department of Insurance examiner request can be answered by reference.
Notify the Controller that the statement-period evidence set is closed.
checklist.done: the filed package is archived under company and period, locked, retention-labelled and indexed for examiner retrieval.

testing.step: Build the population of statutory statements filed for the year
actions: List every writing company from the holding company organisational chart with its NAIC company code, blank type and state of domicile.
For each, list the four filings due for the year — annual plus three quarterlies — and pull the NAIC submission confirmation for each.
Reconcile the count of filings to the count of licensed writing companies and challenge any company with fewer than four filings.
Sign the population as complete and record the extraction date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the population lists every company-period filing with its NAIC confirmation and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the filed blank back to the general ledger independently
actions: Pull the statutory trial balance directly from the GL for the annual statement period rather than accepting the preparer's export.
Recompute total admitted assets, total liabilities, surplus and net income from that TB using the TB-to-blank mapping.
Compare each to the filed Page 2, Page 3 and Page 4 amounts; any difference above $10,000 is an exception with no materiality argument accepted at this stage.
Confirm the mapping file used has not been edited since the filing by checking its version stamp and modification date.
testing.done: independently recomputed statement totals agree to the filed blank within $10,000 or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of blank pages and schedules
actions: Take 100% coverage of Pages 2, 3, 4 and 5 for every writing company's annual blank.
Select 12 supporting schedules at random from the annual blanks using a recorded random seed, forcing inclusion of Schedule D Part 1, Schedule E Part 1 and Schedule T.
Select two quarterly filings per company at random for deadline and signature testing.
Record the population size, seed, selection date and selector in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible from a recorded seed, and covers the four primary pages plus named high-risk schedules.

testing.step: Re-run the NAIC validation edits on the filed data file
actions: Load the archived transmitted data file into the annual statement software as filed and run the full Level 1 and Level 2 validation set.
Compare the resulting edit list to the cross-check clearance log retained by the Statutory Reporting Manager.
Treat any Level 1 edit present in your run but absent from the log, and any Level 2 item filed without an explanation, as an exception.
Screenshot the validation summary into the workpaper as evidence of the re-run.
testing.done: the re-run edit list matches the retained clearance log, or every difference is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Trace reserve and investment amounts to their source systems
actions: Take the Page 3 loss and LAE reserve and trace it to the Appointed Actuary's signed reserve memo and to the reserving system extract behind it.
Take 25 sampled Schedule D Part 1 positions and trace CUSIP, par, book/adjusted carrying value and NAIC designation to the custodian statement and the NAIC designation source.
Confirm the Schedule D summary and Schedule E Part 1 totals equal the Page 2 lines they roll into.
Flag any position whose NAIC designation was internally assigned rather than sourced from NAIC filing exemption data.
testing.done: sampled reserve and investment amounts trace to signed source records with sourced NAIC designations.

testing.step: Recompute filing timeliness against the statutory due dates
actions: Read the NAIC submission timestamp on each sampled filing's confirmation.

Compare it to March 1 for the annual blank and to May 15, August 15 and November 15 for the quarterlies, allowing only the roll-forward the domiciliary state's statute actually grants when the date falls on a weekend.
Compute the days early or late for every filing and tabulate them in the workpaper.
Treat any filing after the statutory date as a reportable breach and confirm whether a late-filing penalty was assessed by the state.
testing.done: days-to-deadline are computed for every sampled filing and every late filing is identified with its penalty status.

testing.step: Verify officer execution and identifier accuracy on the Jurat
actions: Open each sampled Jurat page and confirm the required officer signatures are present, dated on or before the submission date, and notarised where the domiciliary state requires it.
Confirm the signing officers held those offices at the signature date by checking the board-approved officer list held by the Corporate Secretary.
Confirm the NAIC company code, FEIN and state of domicile match the NAIC company demographics of record.
Confirm the named Appointed Actuary matches the person who signed the Statement of Actuarial Opinion filed with the same blank.
testing.done: every sampled Jurat carries valid, dated officer signatures and identifiers that agree to NAIC demographics of record.

testing.step: Confirm the archived filing equals what the NAIC actually holds
actions: Retrieve the archived filed PDF and data file from the repository for each sampled filing.
Compare Pages 2, 3 and 4 line totals to the corresponding filing as it appears in the NAIC Financial Data Repository via iSite+.
Where an amended statement was filed, confirm the amendment is archived alongside the original and that the reason for amendment is documented.
Confirm the folder carries the 7-year retention label and is locked against edit.
testing.done: the archived copy agrees to the NAIC-held filing, amendments are archived with reasons, and retention labelling is in place.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception carrying company code, statement period, page or schedule, and the amount or date in error.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list — mapping error, source extract error, uncleared cross-check, missing signature, late submission, unarchived amendment — and name an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where the blank as filed is wrong, agree with the Controller whether an amended statement must be filed through iSite+ and by when.
Carry every open exception into the next quarterly filing test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and an amendment decision where the filing was wrong.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate by category and compare it to the stated thresholds — zero missed deadlines, zero unsigned Jurats, zero uncleared Level 1 edits.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have the reviewer, who prepared no part of any sampled blank, sign the workpaper and record their independence attestation.
Report the conclusion and any late or amended filings to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and Audit Committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

checklist.step: Publish the submission window plan for the cycle
actions: List every filing due in the cycle by writing company: annual blank, quarterly blank, RBC filing, MCAS blank, and each supplemental with its own date.
For each, record the statutory due date, the internal transmission target set three business days earlier, and the named submitter and backup submitter.
Circulate the plan to the Controller, the Statutory Reporting Manager and the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager for confirmation of readiness dates.
Publish the plan on the filing calendar so every date carries an owner before the cycle opens.
checklist.done: every filing due in the cycle has a due date, an earlier internal transmission target, a named submitter and a backup.

checklist.step: Confirm iSite+ credentials and submitter entitlements before the window opens
actions: Log in to NAIC iSite+ with each named submitter's account and confirm the account is active and not pending password expiry inside the window.
Check each submitter's entitlements cover the applications needed — Financial Data Repository upload and the MCAS application — for every NAIC company code being filed.
Raise missing entitlements with the company's NAIC iSite+ administrator at least 10 business days before the earliest due date, since access provisioning is not same-day.
Record the confirmed submitter, company code and entitlement in the submission register.
checklist.done: every submitter has an active iSite+ account entitled to the right applications and company codes, confirmed before the window.

checklist.step: Run the pre-submission completeness check on each package
actions: Open the filing checklist for the blank type and tick each required component: main blank pages, all schedules and exhibits, Notes, General Interrogatories, supplemental filings and the signed Jurat.
Re-run the software validation and confirm zero Level 1 edits remain in the version about to be transmitted, not in an earlier draft.
Confirm the file version being transmitted carries the same control totals — admitted assets, liabilities, surplus — as the package the CFO signed.
Sign the pre-submission checklist and hand the release to the named submitter.
checklist.done: the exact file about to be transmitted is checklist-complete, edit-clean and matches the signed package control totals.

checklist.step: Transmit the financial blank to the NAIC Financial Data Repository
actions: In NAIC iSite+ open the Financial Data Repository and select the annual or quarterly statement upload for the company code and statement period.
Upload the statement data file produced by the annual statement software together with the PDF of the signed Jurat where the upload requires it.
Wait for the repository to return the processing result rather than closing the browser, and read the record count and any rejection messages returned.
Save the confirmation — confirmation number, company code, period, timestamp — into the submission register and the evidence repository.
checklist.done: the blank is accepted by the Financial Data Repository and a timestamped confirmation is captured in the submission register.

checklist.step: Transmit the MCAS data submission through the iSite+ MCAS application
actions: In iSite+ open the MCAS application and select the data year, the line-of-business blank and the state — for the representative obligation, Idaho.
Upload or key the MCAS data set supplied by the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager and run the application's validation before submitting.
Complete the interrogatories and route the submission to the attesting officer, since MCAS is not filed until the attestation is executed.
Capture the MCAS submission and attestation receipt per state and per line into the submission register.
checklist.done: each MCAS state and line blank is submitted, attested and receipted, with the receipt in the submission register.

checklist.step: Resolve every rejection or validation failure returned by iSite+
actions: Read the rejection message returned by the repository or the MCAS application and record its code and text verbatim in the submission register.
Fix the defect at source — in the GL mapping, the source extract or the MCAS data build — and regenerate the file rather than hand-editing the transmission.
Re-run the pre-submission completeness check on the corrected file before re-transmitting, and re-transmit the same day where the due date is within five business days.
Escalate to the Controller any rejection that cannot be cleared within 24 hours of the due date.
checklist.done: every rejection is recorded with its code, fixed at source, re-transmitted and accepted, with escalations raised where the due date is at risk.

checklist.step: Work the per-state distribution matrix for all 51 jurisdictions
actions: Open the distribution matrix listing, for each of the 51 jurisdictions the company is licensed in, whether NAIC distribution satisfies the state or a direct state filing is also required.
For direct-filing states, record the route the state prescribes — its own electronic portal, email to the financial analysis desk, or a paper original — and the required copies.
Confirm the matrix against each state's current annual filing checklist rather than last year's matrix, since state routes change between cycles.
Mark each jurisdiction row Satisfied-by-NAIC or Direct-filing-required with the source used to decide.
checklist.done: all 51 jurisdiction rows are marked from the state's current checklist with the required route recorded.

checklist.step: Complete the direct state filings the matrix identifies
actions: For each direct-filing state, assemble the state's package — signed original blank, state-specific supplements and the state's transmittal form.
Submit via the route the state prescribes and, where a paper original is required, dispatch by trackable courier so the delivery date is provable.
Record submission date, route, tracking number or portal confirmation, and the recipient on the jurisdiction row.
Chase any state that has not acknowledged within 10 business days and log the chase.
checklist.done: every direct-filing state has a dated, provably delivered submission recorded against its jurisdiction row.

checklist.step: Pay the NAIC and state filing fees and prove payment
actions: Take the fee schedule from the Regulatory Reporting Analyst listing the NAIC database filing fee and each state's annual statement filing fee by company code.
Raise and release payments to hit the state's due date, not the payment run's convenience date, and use the state's required method where it mandates EFT.
Attach the remittance advice and any state fee invoice number to each payment record.
Return payment confirmations to the submission register so fee proof sits with the filing evidence.
checklist.done: every NAIC and state filing fee is paid by its due date with remittance proof filed against the jurisdiction row.

checklist.step: Capture and index every confirmation and acceptance
actions: Save each NAIC confirmation, MCAS attestation receipt, state portal confirmation and state acceptance letter as a separate PDF named company-jurisdiction-filing-period.
Index each by NAIC company code, jurisdiction, filing type, period and submission timestamp.
Mark the jurisdiction row Confirmed only when a confirmation document exists — an entry in a spreadsheet is not evidence of acceptance.
Report any jurisdiction still unconfirmed five business days after the due date to the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
checklist.done: every jurisdiction row is either Confirmed with an attached confirmation document or reported as unconfirmed.

checklist.step: Reconcile the submission register to the filing plan and close the cycle
actions: Compare the submission register line by line to the cycle plan and identify any planned filing with no submission event.
Confirm each company code filed the correct blank type and period, and that no company was filed twice for the same period without an amendment reason.
Compute on-time percentage by jurisdiction and by filing type for the cycle.
Sign the cycle closure statement and issue it to the Controller and the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: the register reconciles to the plan with no unfiled item, and a signed cycle closure statement with on-time percentages has been issued.

checklist.step: Notify the state and log the breach when a deadline is missed
actions: Open a breach issue the same business day a statutory due date passes without an accepted submission, naming the jurisdiction, company code and filing.
Draft the notification to the state's financial analysis or market conduct desk stating the cause and the committed filing date, and route it to the Head of Compliance for clearance before sending.
Record any late-filing penalty assessed by the state and route it for payment and for GL accrual.
Set a remediation action addressing the cause, not the symptom, with an owner and a date.
checklist.done: every missed deadline has a same-day breach issue, a cleared state notification, penalty tracking and an owned remediation action.

checklist.step: Handle amended and corrected filings through the same controlled route
actions: Where a filed statement or MCAS submission is found to be wrong, document the error, the corrected figures and the surplus or ratio impact before touching iSite+.
Obtain Controller approval to amend, then upload the amended filing to the Financial Data Repository or resubmit the MCAS blank marked as an amendment.
Notify every jurisdiction that received the original filing that an amendment has been made and what changed.
File the original, the amendment and the notification together so the audit trail shows both versions.
checklist.done: amendments are approved, resubmitted through iSite+, notified to affected states, and archived alongside the originals.

checklist.step: Refresh the distribution matrix from state checklists for the next cycle
actions: Collect each state's current annual filing checklist and bulletin updates as they are published for the coming statement year.
Compare each state's requirements to the current matrix row and mark added, removed or re-routed requirements.
Circulate a change summary to the Regulatory Reporting Manager and the Controller before the next cycle plan is built.
Version the matrix with an effective statement year so it is clear which cycle each row governed.
checklist.done: a versioned, state-sourced distribution matrix for the next statement year has been issued with a change summary.

checklist.step: Retain the cycle evidence set for the retention period
actions: Close the cycle folder containing the submission register, all confirmations, fee proofs, state acceptance letters and any breach notifications.
Apply the 7-year retention label and lock the folder against further edit.
Confirm the folder is retrievable by jurisdiction, company code, filing type and period.
Confirm closure to the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
checklist.done: the cycle evidence set is locked, retention-labelled and retrievable by jurisdiction, company and filing type.

testing.step: Build the population of filings that were due in the cycle
actions: Take the writing company list and the licensed-jurisdiction list from the NAIC company demographics of record rather than from the filing team's plan.
Derive the expected filing events for the cycle: blank x company x period, plus RBC and MCAS obligations, plus every direct-filing jurisdiction on the matrix.
Compare the derived expectation to the submission register and list every expected filing with no register entry.
Sign the population as complete and record its derivation in the workpaper.
testing.done: an independently derived population of expected filings exists and every gap against the register is listed.

testing.step: Reconcile the submission register to NAIC-held records
actions: For each register row, locate the filing in NAIC iSite+ — the Financial Data Repository entry or the MCAS submission record for the state and data year.
Compare the confirmation number, company code, period and submission timestamp to what the register claims.
Treat any register row with no matching NAIC record, or a timestamp differing from the register, as an exception.
Record the reconciliation in the workpaper with the NAIC record references used.
testing.done: every register row is matched to an NAIC-held record with agreeing confirmation number and timestamp, or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Draw the jurisdiction sample and document the method
actions: Take 100% of direct-filing jurisdictions and 100% of MCAS states filed in the cycle.
Select 20 further jurisdiction-filing rows at random from the Satisfied-by-NAIC population using a recorded seed.
Force inclusion of any jurisdiction that produced an exception in the prior cycle.
Record population size, seed, selection date and selector so the sample is reproducible.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all direct-filing and MCAS jurisdictions plus prior-exception states is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the distribution decision against the state's own checklist
actions: For each sampled jurisdiction, open that state's current annual filing checklist or filing bulletin without first reading the matrix row.
Reach your own conclusion on whether NAIC distribution alone satisfies the state or a direct filing, fee or paper original is required.
Compare your conclusion to the matrix row; a right answer supported by a stale or wrong source is still an exception.
Capture the checklist page you relied on, dated, into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled jurisdiction has an independent distribution conclusion and a dated source capture.

testing.step: Trace each sampled filing to a retained confirmation document
actions: Retrieve the confirmation artefact for each sampled row — NAIC confirmation, MCAS attestation receipt, state portal confirmation, courier delivery proof or state acceptance letter.
Confirm the artefact names the right company code, jurisdiction, filing type and period.
Treat a register entry with no retrievable confirmation document as an unevidenced filing, regardless of the team's recollection.
Note the repository path of every artefact examined in the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled row has a retrievable confirmation naming the correct company, jurisdiction, filing type and period.

testing.step: Recompute timeliness against each jurisdiction's own due date
actions: For each sampled row, take the statutory due date from the state checklist — March 1 for the annual blank, the quarterly 15ths, April 30 for MCAS — rather than from the internal calendar.
Compute days early or late using the acceptance timestamp on the confirmation, not the upload attempt time.
Where an initial upload was rejected, use the timestamp of the accepted resubmission as the filing date.
Tabulate the timeliness result and flag every row filed after its own jurisdiction's date.
testing.done: days-to-deadline are recomputed from state-sourced due dates and acceptance timestamps for every sampled row.

testing.step: Test rejection handling and resubmission integrity
actions: Pull every rejection recorded in the cycle and read the rejection code and text captured against it.
Confirm the corrected file was regenerated from source and check the control totals of the accepted file against the CFO-signed package.
Confirm no accepted file differs from the signed package without a documented amendment approval from the Controller.
Flag any rejection with no recorded root cause or with a hand-edited transmission file.
testing.done: every rejection has a recorded code, a source-level fix, and an accepted file whose control totals match the signed package.

testing.step: Test fee payment and proof for the sampled jurisdictions
actions: Take the fee schedule for the cycle and, for each sampled jurisdiction, trace the payment to a cleared disbursement in the ledger.
Compare the payment date to the state's fee due date and the amount to the state's published fee for that company type.
Confirm the payment method matched any state mandate for EFT.
Flag unpaid, underpaid or late fees as exceptions and confirm whether the state assessed a penalty.
testing.done: every sampled jurisdiction's filing fee traces to a cleared payment of the right amount, method and date.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying jurisdiction, company code, filing type, period and the specific failure.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list — entitlement lapse, stale distribution matrix, rejection unresolved, fee missed, confirmation not retained, late transmission — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for missed jurisdictions, confirm the filing has since been accepted and the state notified.
Carry every open issue into the next cycle's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute on-time percentage and unevidenced-filing count against the zero-tolerance thresholds.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, citing the workpaper references.
Have the reviewer, who holds no iSite+ submitter credential and transmitted none of the sampled filings, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with on-time percentage, exception count, stated conclusion and committee reporting date is filed.

In-scope systems.value: Annual statement software schedule modules fed by the investment book of record, the reinsurance administration system, the reserving system and the policy admin extract

Compliance procedure documented.value: Supplemental Schedules Preparation Procedure — schedule owner matrix, source-system extract specifications, schedule-to-page cross-check list and the supplemental filing calendar

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Controller; refreshed each year against the NAIC's adopted schedule and instruction changes before the close begins

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Schedules file with the annual blank on March 1; Actuarial Opinion March 1, Actuarial Opinion Summary March 15, RBC March 1, and the April 1 supplementals including the Accident and Health Policy Experience Exhibit

Deadline reminders configured.value: One calendar task per schedule with its own owner, alerting at T-15 and T-5 days to March 1, plus separate tasks for the March 15 and April 1 supplementals

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Controller signs off any schedule filed with an unresolved difference and every re-filed schedule

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Every required schedule present; schedule totals must equal the blank page line they support to the dollar; any omitted schedule or supplemental, or any unexplained difference, is a fail

checklist.step: Build the required schedule inventory for each blank type
actions: Open the NAIC Annual Statement Instructions for each blank the group files (P&C, Life/Fraternal, Health, Title) and list every schedule and exhibit that blank requires.
Mark each schedule required, not applicable with the reason, or newly added this statement year.

Assign a named preparer and reviewer to every schedule — investments to Investment Operations, reinsurance to the Reinsurance Accountant, loss development to the Reserving Actuary, taxes to the Tax Manager.
Publish the inventory with owner and due date to the close calendar before the close begins.
checklist.done: an owner-assigned schedule inventory exists per blank type with not-applicable calls reasoned and dated.

checklist.step: Prepare the real estate, mortgage and other invested asset schedules
actions: Extract real estate holdings for Schedule A with acquisition date, cost, encumbrances, depreciation and book/adjusted carrying value per property.
Extract mortgage loans for Schedule B with loan number, property type, interest rate, maturity, and any loans 90 days overdue or in foreclosure, which must be shown separately.
Extract other long-term invested assets for Schedule BA including joint ventures, partnerships and surplus notes, with the SSAP No. 48 measurement basis for each.
Reconcile each schedule total to the corresponding Page 2 asset line and pass the tie-out to the Senior Accountant.
checklist.done: Schedules A, B and BA are complete with overdue and foreclosure loans shown separately and each total tied to Page 2.

checklist.step: Prepare the bond, stock and short-term investment schedules
actions: Build Schedule D Part 1 (bonds) and Part 2 (stocks) at CUSIP level with par, book/adjusted carrying value, fair value, effective rate, acquisition date and NAIC designation.
Build Schedule D Parts 3, 4 and 5 for acquisitions, disposals and non-cash transfers during the year, and confirm the year's activity reconciles beginning to ending carrying value.
Build Schedule DA for short-term investments and Schedule DB for derivatives, including hedge documentation status under SSAP No. 86 for every open position.
Confirm every bond carries an NAIC designation sourced from NAIC filing exemption or SVO data and escalate undesignated holdings to the Controller.
checklist.done: Schedule D Parts 1-5, DA and DB are complete, designation-sourced, and roll forward from prior-year carrying value.

checklist.step: Prepare the cash and deposit schedule and tie it to the banks
actions: Build Schedule E Part 1 listing every depository with its balance at year end, and Part 2 for cash equivalents.
Tie every depository balance to the December bank reconciliation and confirm no account is omitted by comparing to the treasury account inventory.
Identify any balance held under a custodial or trust agreement and confirm the agreement is disclosed in the General Interrogatories.
Pass the reconciled schedule and the supporting bank reconciliations to the Senior Accountant.
checklist.done: Schedule E lists every depository, ties to bank reconciliations, and custodial arrangements are cross-referenced to the interrogatories.

checklist.step: Prepare the reinsurance schedule and the provision for reinsurance
actions: Extract ceded and assumed balances by reinsurer for the reinsurance schedule (Schedule F for P&C blanks, Schedule S for life blanks) with each reinsurer's NAIC company code or ID number.

Classify each reinsurer as authorised, unauthorised, certified or reciprocal jurisdiction using the state's current list, and record collateral held — letters of credit, funds withheld, trust balances — per reinsurer.
Compute the provision for reinsurance from overdue recoverables and uncollateralised unauthorised balances and carry it to the Page 3 liability line and the surplus roll-forward.
Confirm slow-paying balances over 90 days with the Reinsurance Manager and document the collection status of each.
checklist.done: the reinsurance schedule is complete by reinsurer with authorisation status, collateral and a computed provision carried to Page 3.

checklist.step: Prepare the loss development exhibit and its accident year triangles
actions: Build Schedule P Parts 1 through 7 by line of business and accident year: premiums earned, loss and DCC payments, case reserves, bulk and IBNR reserves and claim counts.
Confirm the current accident year row in Schedule P agrees to the current-year incurred losses on Page 4 and the total reserve agrees to Page 3.
Populate the one-year and two-year development columns and prepare the written explanation for any adverse development exceeding 5% of surplus, which the state analyst will ask about.
Have the Appointed Actuary review the triangles against the reserve analysis before the schedule is locked.
checklist.done: Schedule P triangles tie to Pages 3 and 4, development columns are populated, and material adverse development has a written explanation.

checklist.step: Prepare the premiums and losses by state exhibit and the reinsurance premium reconciliation
actions: Extract direct written premium, direct earned premium, dividends, direct losses paid, direct losses incurred and direct losses unpaid by state of risk.
Populate Schedule T and the Exhibit of Premiums and Losses for each of the 51 jurisdictions plus alien business, and confirm the grand total ties to the Underwriting and Investment Exhibit.
Reconcile direct to net premium through the ceded and assumed premium in the reinsurance schedule, documenting each reconciling item.
Confirm each state showing premium is on the Jurat licensed-state list and refer any exception to the Compliance Officer.
checklist.done: state premium and loss detail ties to the underwriting exhibit and reconciles direct to net through the reinsurance schedule.

checklist.step: Prepare the holding company organisational schedule
actions: Build Schedule Y Part 1 as the organisational chart showing every entity in the insurance holding company system with ownership percentages and NAIC company codes or FEINs.
Build Part 2 listing all intercompany agreements and transactions during the year — management fees, tax sharing, pooling, cost allocation — with the amounts settled.
Confirm each disclosed agreement has been filed with and non-disapproved by the domiciliary state under the holding company act, and attach the approval reference.
Reconcile the intercompany amounts to the related party note and to the intercompany balances in the ledger.
checklist.done: Schedule Y shows the full group structure and every intercompany agreement with its state approval reference and settled amount.

checklist.step: Prepare the investment income, expense and tax exhibits
actions: Build the Exhibit of Net Investment Income and the Exhibit of Capital Gains (Losses), tying investment income earned to the Page 4 line and to the investment accounting feed.
Build the Underwriting and Investment Exhibit parts covering premiums written and earned, losses paid and incurred, and expenses by category.
Obtain the Tax Manager's current and deferred tax computation with the SSAP No. 101 admissibility test and populate the tax exhibit and the income tax note.
Tie every exhibit total to the page line it supports and record each tie in the schedule tie-out workbook.
checklist.done: income, gain, underwriting and tax exhibits are complete, tax-supported and tied to their supporting page lines.

checklist.step: Run the schedule-to-page cross-checks across the whole blank
actions: Run the statement software's schedule cross-check set covering Schedule D to Page 2, Schedule E to the cash line, the reinsurance schedule to the recoverable and provision lines, Schedule P to Pages 3 and 4, and Schedule T to the underwriting exhibit.
Resolve every difference in the source extract rather than by overriding the schedule.
Where an instruction genuinely permits a difference, record the instruction reference and the amount on the tie-out workbook.
Print the cross-check report and attach it to the schedule tie-out workbook.
checklist.done: all schedule-to-page cross-checks clear, with any permitted difference supported by an instruction reference.

checklist.step: Capture preparer and reviewer sign-off on every schedule
actions: Require the named preparer and a second reviewer to sign each schedule tie-out sheet with the source extract reference and extract date.
Reject any schedule signed by a single person or supported by an extract dated before the GL close.
Review the schedules carrying the most judgement — the reinsurance provision, Schedule BA valuations, Schedule P development — personally before sign-off.
Record the sign-off status of every schedule on the inventory before the blank is released for filing.
checklist.done: every schedule on the inventory carries dual preparer and reviewer sign-off against a post-close source extract.

checklist.step: Prepare and file the March 1 supplemental filings
actions: Assemble the supplementals due with the annual statement on March 1: the Statement of Actuarial Opinion, the Risk-Based Capital filing, the Supplemental Compensation Exhibit and the Investment Risk Interrogatories.
Confirm the RBC filing's inputs — reserves, invested asset designations, premium — agree to the filed blank, since RBC is derived from it.
Upload each supplemental to the Financial Data Repository under the correct filing type and capture the confirmation.
Diarise the Actuarial Opinion Summary for March 15, which is a separate, later filing and is routinely missed.
checklist.done: all March 1 supplementals are filed with RBC inputs agreeing to the blank, and the March 15 opinion summary is diarised.

checklist.step: Prepare and file the April 1 and later supplementals
actions: List the supplementals due after the blank — including the Accident and Health Policy Experience Exhibit and the line-specific supplements the blank type requires — with their April 1 or later dates.
Collect the source data from the owning team (health experience data from Actuarial, long-term care data from Product) against a written extract specification.
File each through the Financial Data Repository on its own due date and capture the confirmation separately from the March 1 confirmations.
Update the schedule inventory to show each supplemental as filed with its confirmation reference.
checklist.done: every post-blank supplemental is filed on its own due date with a separately captured confirmation.

checklist.step: Explain the analytical ratios the state analyst will compute from the schedules
actions: Recompute the IRIS ratios and the key schedule-driven measures — two-year reserve development to surplus, ceded reinsurance leverage, investments in affiliates to surplus.
Identify each ratio falling outside the usual range and draft the explanation with the underlying schedule reference.
Review the drafts with the Controller and the Appointed Actuary before the annual statement is filed, not after the state asks.
File the explanations with the statement working papers so an analyst inquiry can be answered from the file.
checklist.done: every out-of-range analytical ratio has a pre-drafted, schedule-referenced explanation on file before the analyst asks.

checklist.step: Archive schedule source extracts and tie-outs as retained evidence
actions: File each schedule's source extract, tie-out sheet and dual sign-off under company code, statement year and schedule name.
Include the cross-check report, the ratio explanations and the supplemental filing confirmations in the same folder.
Apply the 7-year retention label and lock the folder against edit.
Confirm to the Controller that the schedule evidence set is complete against the schedule inventory.
checklist.done: every inventory schedule has an archived, locked evidence set including extract, tie-out and sign-off.

testing.step: Build the population of schedules required for the statement year
actions: Derive the required schedule list independently from the current NAIC Annual Statement Instructions for each blank type filed, rather than from the team's inventory.
Compare the derived list to the schedule inventory and list any schedule the inventory omits or marks not applicable.
Add the March 1, March 15 and April 1 supplementals to the population.
Sign the population as complete with the instruction edition used recorded in the workpaper.
testing.done: an instruction-derived schedule and supplemental population exists and every omission or not-applicable call is listed for challenge.

testing.step: Reconcile every schedule total to the blank page it supports
actions: Open the filed blank and recompute each schedule-to-page tie: Schedule D to Page 2, Schedule E to cash, the reinsurance schedule to recoverables and the provision, Schedule P to Pages 3 and 4, Schedule T to the underwriting exhibit.
Compare each recomputed tie to the tie-out workbook and treat any difference not supported by a cited instruction as an exception.
Confirm the tie-out sheets were signed by two people and dated after the GL close.
Record every tie result, agreeing or not, in the workpaper.
testing.done: every schedule-to-page tie is independently recomputed and any unsupported difference is logged.

testing.step: Draw and document the schedule sample
actions: Take 100% of the judgement-heavy schedules: the reinsurance schedule, Schedule BA, Schedule P and Schedule Y.
Select six further schedules at random from the remaining inventory using a recorded seed.
Within Schedule D, select 30 positions at random for line-level testing.
Record population size, seed, selection date and selector so the sample is reproducible.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all judgement-heavy schedules plus random coverage and 30 Schedule D positions is documented.

testing.step: Trace sampled schedule lines to the source system of record
actions: For the 30 sampled Schedule D positions, trace CUSIP, par, book/adjusted carrying value, fair value and acquisition date to the investment book of record and the custodian statement.
For sampled reinsurance schedule rows, trace ceded balances and collateral to the reinsurance administration system and the letter of credit or trust confirmation.
For sampled Schedule B rows, confirm loans over 90 days overdue are reported in the overdue category.
Flag any line whose schedule value was manually adjusted without a documented reconciling entry.
testing.done: sampled schedule lines trace to source-system and custodian or reinsurer records with manual adjustments identified.

testing.step: Re-perform the reinsurance provision computation
actions: Take the reinsurer-level balances, ageing and collateral from the reinsurance schedule and recompute the provision for reinsurance under the schedule instructions.
Independently check each reinsurer's authorisation status against the domiciliary state's current list of authorised, certified and reciprocal jurisdiction reinsurers as at the statement date.
Compare the recomputed provision to the amount carried on Page 3 and in the surplus roll-forward.
Treat a misclassified reinsurer as an exception even where the provision total happens to agree.
testing.done: the provision for reinsurance is independently recomputed, authorisation statuses verified, and differences logged.

testing.step: Re-perform the loss development exhibit ties and development disclosure
actions: Take the reserving system's accident-year output at the valuation date and compare paid loss, case reserve and IBNR by accident year to Schedule P.
Recompute the one-year and two-year development amounts and express them as a percentage of surplus.
Where development exceeds 5% of surplus, confirm a written explanation exists in the working papers and was prepared before filing.
Confirm the Statement of Actuarial Opinion covers the reserve amounts shown in the schedule.
testing.done: Schedule P agrees to the reserving system, development is recomputed, and material development carries a pre-filing explanation.

testing.step: Test the holding company schedule against corporate records
actions: Compare the Schedule Y organisational chart to the corporate register held by the Corporate Secretary, entity by entity and ownership percentage by percentage.
For each disclosed intercompany agreement, obtain the domiciliary state's non-disapproval or approval reference and confirm the agreement's terms match what is disclosed.
Reconcile the reported intercompany settled amounts to the ledger intercompany accounts.
Flag any entity present in the corporate register but absent from Schedule Y.
testing.done: Schedule Y agrees to the corporate register, intercompany agreements carry state approval references, and amounts tie to the ledger.

testing.step: Recompute supplemental filing timeliness
actions: For each supplemental in the population, retrieve its Financial Data Repository confirmation and read the acceptance timestamp.
Compare to its own due date — March 1 for the Actuarial Opinion and RBC, March 15 for the Actuarial Opinion Summary, April 1 for the experience exhibits.
Confirm the RBC filing's reserve, premium and asset inputs agree to the filed annual blank.
Flag any supplemental with no confirmation or an acceptance timestamp after its date.
testing.done: each supplemental has a confirmation, a computed days-to-deadline result, and RBC inputs agreeing to the filed blank.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming company code, statement year, schedule or supplemental and the amount or date in error.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list — schedule omitted, extract wrong, tie-out unsigned, misclassification, late supplemental, unsupported manual adjustment — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where the filed schedule is wrong, agree with the Controller whether an amended filing is required and by when.
Carry every open issue into next year's schedule test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and an amendment decision where the schedule was wrong.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Summarise schedules tested, ties recomputed, exceptions by category and their aggregate dollar effect on surplus.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, citing workpaper references.
Have the reviewer, who prepared none of the sampled schedules and does not report to a schedule owner, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with schedule coverage, exception summary, stated conclusion and committee reporting date is filed.
