checklist.step: Confirm which companies owe an audited statutory statement and which exemptions apply
actions: List every writing company with its direct written and assumed premium for the year and its licensed jurisdictions.
Apply the domiciliary state's audit requirement, checking whether any small-company exemption threshold is met and whether the state has granted it in writing.
Confirm any claimed exemption has a written state approval letter on file — an untested assumption of exemption is the common failure here.
Publish the audited-entity list with the audit scope and the exemption evidence to the Audit Committee before planning starts.
checklist.done: the audited-entity list is issued with every exemption supported by a written state approval on file.

checklist.step: Confirm the auditor's engagement, qualifications and independence
actions: Obtain the CPA firm's written representation that it and its engagement personnel are independent under the domiciliary state's audit regulation and the AICPA rules.
Confirm the lead and concurring audit partner rotation limits have not been breached and record the years each partner has served on the engagement.

Confirm no prohibited non-audit services — bookkeeping, actuarial services relating to the statutory reserves, internal audit outsourcing — were provided, and that any permitted non-audit service was pre-approved by the Audit Committee.
Obtain and file the CPA awareness letter, which the state requires by December 31 of the year being audited.
checklist.done: an independence representation, partner-rotation record, pre-approval log and a December-dated awareness letter are on file.

checklist.step: Agree the audit plan, scope and the prepared-by-client calendar
actions: Hold the planning meeting with the engagement partner and agree materiality, significant risk areas — reserves, reinsurance recoverables, investment valuation, premium recognition — and the interim and final fieldwork dates.
Load the PBC request list into the audit workflow with an owner and a due date for every item, backing off from a mid-May draft-report date so June 1 is not the first checkpoint.
Assign the actuarial deliverables to the Appointed Actuary and the reinsurance deliverables to the Reinsurance Accountant explicitly, since those items drive the critical path.
Circulate the agreed plan and calendar to the Audit Committee chair.
checklist.done: an agreed audit plan and an owner-and-date PBC calendar exist, working back from a mid-May draft report.

checklist.step: Deliver the PBC evidence and track the request list to closure
actions: Upload each requested schedule, reconciliation and supporting document against its request-list item, naming the source system and extract date on every file.
Hold a twice-weekly status call with the engagement team while fieldwork is open and re-date any slipping item with a named reason.
Escalate any item more than five business days overdue to the Controller, since PBC slippage is the usual cause of a late June 1 filing.
Close each request only when the auditor marks it received and sufficient.
checklist.done: every PBC item is auditor-closed or has a re-dated plan with a named owner and reason.

checklist.step: Support the reserve, reinsurance and investment audit areas
actions: Provide the auditor's actuarial specialist with the reserve analysis, data reconciliation to the statutory blank and the methodology and assumption documentation supporting the Statement of Actuarial Opinion.
Have the Reinsurance Accountant provide the reinsurer-level recoverable ageing, collateral evidence and the provision for reinsurance computation.
Have the Investment Operations Manager provide the custodian confirmation, fair value hierarchy support and NAIC designation sources for Schedule D positions.
Log every auditor question and its written answer so the audit file and the company file say the same thing.
checklist.done: the reserve, reinsurance and investment areas are supported with reconciled data and a logged question-and-answer trail.

checklist.step: Evaluate, post and disclose audit adjustments
actions: Take the auditor's summary of adjustments — both corrected and uncorrected — and record each with its effect on admitted assets, liabilities, surplus and net income.
Decide and document, per adjustment, whether it is posted or passed, with the rationale for each passed item and its aggregate effect on surplus.
Post the accepted adjustments in the statutory ledger and determine whether the already-filed annual blank must be amended through iSite+ as a result.
Present the summary of uncorrected misstatements to the Audit Committee with the surplus impact stated as a percentage.
checklist.done: every audit adjustment is posted or reasoned as passed, with the surplus impact quantified and reported to the Audit Committee.

checklist.step: Prepare the audited statutory financial statements for issue
actions: Compile the audited statutory statements on the statutory basis of accounting: balance sheet, statement of operations, changes in capital and surplus, cash flow and the notes.
Reconcile the audited statements to the filed annual blank and prepare the schedule explaining every difference caused by a post-filing audit adjustment.
Confirm the notes include the required statutory disclosures — permitted or prescribed practices with their state approval, reinsurance, related parties and subsequent events.
Circulate the draft to the Controller and the engagement partner for the final read before opinion issue.
checklist.done: audited statements are compiled on the statutory basis, reconciled to the filed blank with every difference explained.

checklist.step: Obtain the signed audit opinion and the management representation letter
actions: Review the draft opinion and confirm the opinion type — unmodified, qualified, adverse or disclaimer — and that it names the statutory basis as the applicable framework.
Sign the management representation letter dated the same day as the opinion, after confirming with the Controller that every representation is supported.
Escalate to the Audit Committee chair immediately if any modification to the opinion is proposed, since a modified statutory opinion triggers state attention.
Obtain the signed opinion in PDF with the firm's manual or authorised electronic signature.
checklist.done: a signed opinion and a same-dated management representation letter are held, with any modification escalated to the Audit Committee.

checklist.step: File the audited statutory report by June 1
actions: In NAIC iSite+ open the Financial Data Repository and upload the audited statutory financial report under the audited-report filing type for the company code and year.
Work the distribution matrix for jurisdictions that require a direct copy or a state-specific transmittal alongside NAIC distribution and submit those on the same day.
Confirm the June 1 date, and where the domiciliary state has granted a written extension, file the extension approval with the submission evidence.
Capture the confirmation for every jurisdiction into the submission register.
checklist.done: the audited report is accepted by the Financial Data Repository and by every direct-filing jurisdiction on or before June 1.

checklist.step: Obtain and file the auditor's internal control communication by August 1
actions: Request the Communication of Internal Control Related Matters Noted in an Audit from the engagement partner, covering any material weakness identified, or a statement that none were identified.
Prepare management's written response to each material weakness or significant deficiency with a named remediation owner and date.
File the communication with the domiciliary state and with any other state requiring it by August 1, capturing the confirmation for each.
Table the communication and management's response at the next Audit Committee meeting.
checklist.done: the internal control communication and management's response are filed by August 1 with confirmations captured.

checklist.step: Produce Management's Report of Internal Control over Financial Reporting where required
actions: Determine whether the company exceeds the direct and assumed premium threshold in the state's audit regulation that triggers the management internal control report.
Where triggered, document the control framework used, the scoping of significant accounts and processes, the testing performed and the conclusion on effectiveness as at December 31.
Have the CFO and the Controller sign the report and file it by August 1 with the domiciliary state.
Where the threshold is not met, document the premium computation supporting that determination and retain it.
checklist.done: either a signed management internal control report is filed by August 1, or a retained computation supports the non-applicability call.

checklist.step: Handle a change of auditor within the notification deadlines
actions: On any dismissal or resignation of the CPA firm, notify the domiciliary commissioner in writing within 5 business days of the event.

Within 10 business days of that notification, send the commissioner the letter stating whether, in the 24 months before the change, there were any disagreements on accounting, auditing scope or disclosure, and the nature of each.
Obtain the outgoing firm's letter stating whether it agrees with the company's statement and forward it to the commissioner.
Record the Audit Committee resolution approving the new firm's appointment and confirm the new firm's independence before engagement.
checklist.done: auditor changes are notified within 5 business days, the disagreements letter is sent within 10, and the successor firm's independence is confirmed.

checklist.step: Report an adverse financial condition finding to the commissioner immediately
actions: Where the CPA determines the insurer has materially misstated its financial condition or does not meet minimum capital and surplus requirements, notify the board in writing.
Notify the domiciliary commissioner in writing within 5 business days of receiving the CPA's determination.
Confirm the CPA's own obligation to notify the commissioner has been met and that the two notifications are consistent.
Open a board-level remediation item with the CFO and the Chief Risk Officer named as owners.
checklist.done: any adverse-condition determination is notified to the board and the commissioner within 5 business days with an owned remediation item.

checklist.step: Track remediation of every reported control deficiency to closure
actions: Open a remediation item for every material weakness and significant deficiency in the internal control communication, with the control, the owner and the target date.
Require the owner to evidence the redesigned control and to run it for at least one cycle before closure is requested.
Re-test each remediated control independently before marking it closed and record the test evidence.
Report open items and ageing to the Audit Committee each quarter until they are closed.
checklist.done: every reported deficiency has an owned, re-tested remediation item reported quarterly until closed.

checklist.step: Archive the audit evidence set for the retention period
actions: File the signed opinion, audited statements, management representation letter, awareness letter, independence representation, adjustment summary, internal control communication and all filing confirmations under company code and audit year.
Include the blank-to-audited-statements reconciliation and any exemption approval letters.
Apply the 7-year retention label and lock the folder against edit.
Confirm the set is complete against the audited-entity list and notify the Controller.
checklist.done: a complete, locked, retention-labelled audit evidence set exists for every entity on the audited-entity list.

testing.step: Build the population of entities owing an audited statutory statement
actions: Derive the population from the licensed writing companies and their filed annual statement premium, independently of the Controller's audited-entity list.
Apply the domiciliary state's audit regulation thresholds yourself to determine which entities owe an audited report.
Compare your derived list to the audited-entity list and challenge every difference, especially entities treated as exempt.
Sign the population as complete and record the regulation edition and threshold used.
testing.done: an independently derived audited-entity population exists and every exemption or omission is challenged.

testing.step: Reconcile the audited statements to the filed annual blank
actions: Compare admitted assets, liabilities, surplus and net income in the audited statements to the same figures in the annual blank filed on March 1.
Trace each difference to a specific audit adjustment on the adjustment summary and confirm it was posted in the ledger.
Where a difference is material to surplus, confirm an amended blank was filed through iSite+ or that a documented decision not to amend was approved by the Controller.
Record the full reconciliation in the workpaper with each difference explained.
testing.done: every difference between the audited statements and the filed blank is traced to a posted adjustment with an amendment decision.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of adjustments and control items
actions: Take 100% of audit adjustments over 1% of surplus and 100% of uncorrected misstatements.
Select 10 further adjustments at random from the remainder using a recorded seed.
Take 100% of material weaknesses and significant deficiencies reported in the internal control communication.
Record population size, seed, selection date and selector so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all large and uncorrected adjustments and all reported deficiencies is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the independence and rotation assessment
actions: Read the domiciliary state's audit regulation independence provisions directly, then assess the engagement without first reading the firm's representation.
Check the lead and concurring partner tenure against the rotation limit using the engagement letters for the prior years.
List every non-audit service the firm billed in the year from the accounts payable vendor detail and test each against the prohibited-services list and the Audit Committee pre-approval log.
Treat any prohibited service, any missing pre-approval and any tenure breach as an exception regardless of the firm's own conclusion.
testing.done: independence and partner rotation are independently assessed against the regulation and the billed-services detail.

testing.step: Trace sampled audit adjustments into the ledger and the statements
actions: For each sampled posted adjustment, locate the journal entry in the statutory ledger with its posting date, preparer and approver.
Confirm the posted amount and account agree to the adjustment summary and flow into the audited statement line.
For each passed adjustment, confirm a written rationale exists and that the aggregate of passed items was presented to the Audit Committee.
Flag any adjustment posted without a second-person approval.
testing.done: sampled adjustments trace to approved journal entries or to a documented pass rationale reported to the Audit Committee.

testing.step: Recompute the filing deadline results for the audit deliverables
actions: Retrieve the iSite+ and state confirmations for the audited report, the internal control communication and, where applicable, the management internal control report.
Compare the acceptance timestamps to June 1 and August 1 and compute days early or late for each entity and jurisdiction.
Confirm the awareness letter is dated on or before December 31 of the audited year.
Where an extension was used, confirm a written state approval exists and pre-dates the original due date.
testing.done: days-to-deadline are computed for every audit deliverable, with extensions supported by pre-dated written state approvals.

testing.step: Test the internal control communication and management's response
actions: Read the communication issued by the CPA and list every material weakness and significant deficiency it names.
Confirm each has a management response with a named owner and target date, and a remediation item open in the control workflow.
For items marked remediated, obtain the re-test evidence and confirm the control ran for at least one cycle before closure.
Flag any deficiency closed on assertion alone with no re-test evidence.
testing.done: every reported deficiency has an owned response and, where closed, re-test evidence covering at least one operating cycle.

testing.step: Verify the opinion, representation letter and auditor-change notifications
actions: Confirm the retained opinion is signed, names the statutory basis of accounting, and is dated on or before the June 1 filing.
Confirm the management representation letter carries the CFO signature and the same date as the opinion.
Where the CPA firm changed in the period, confirm the 5-business-day commissioner notification and the 10-business-day disagreements letter were sent, and read the outgoing firm's response letter.
Confirm the Audit Committee minutes record the appointment resolution and the independence confirmation.
testing.done: the opinion, representation letter and any auditor-change notifications are verified as signed, dated and timely.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the entity, audit year, deliverable and the specific failure.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list — PBC slippage, unsupported exemption, independence breach, unposted adjustment, late filing, unevidenced remediation — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for a late or unfiled deliverable, confirm the state has been notified and by whom.
Carry every open issue into next year's audit test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a state-notification status where a filing was missed.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report to the Audit Committee
actions: Summarise entities in scope, deliverables filed on time, adjustment effect on surplus and exceptions by category.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, citing the workpaper references.
Have the reviewer, who sits outside the finance reporting line and coordinated none of the audit, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, surplus impact and Audit Committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the 51-jurisdiction filing calendar and the timeliness evidence; each calendar row carries a named preparer and submitter

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — each jurisdiction's annual and quarterly filing statute and its current filing checklist, re-read each statement year before the calendar is baselined (rep: Alaska Statutes Title 21; also Alabama Title 27 and the Arkansas Insurance Code)

In-scope processes.value: Continuous maintenance of the filing calendar covering every NAIC and state filing obligation across the 51 jurisdictions — annual and quarterly blanks, supplementals, RBC, MCAS, audited report, holding company filings — and the capture of timeliness evidence for each

In-scope systems.value: Filing calendar of record with per-obligation owners, due dates and reminders; timeliness evidence held in the compliance evidence repository and cross-referenced to iSite+ confirmations

Compliance procedure documented.value: Filing Calendar Maintenance Procedure — annual baseline from state checklists, in-year change intake from bulletins, owner assignment, reminder configuration, timeliness evidence capture and monthly reconciliation

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Controller; re-approved each statement year at baseline and on any material change to a state's filing regime

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: All of them, by definition — the calendar is the control: March 1 annual and RBC, March 15 opinion summary, April 1 supplementals, April 30 MCAS, May 15 / August 15 / November 15 quarterlies, June 1 audited report, August 1 internal control communication, plus state-specific dates

Deadline reminders configured.value: Every calendar row carries T-30, T-14, T-5 and T-1 reminders to the named preparer, with an unacknowledged T-5 reminder auto-escalating to the Regulatory Reporting Manager and an unacknowledged T-1 to the Controller

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Baselined calendar versions, state checklist sources, reminder and acknowledgement logs, submission confirmations and the monthly reconciliation retained 7 years in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Missing calendar rows, unowned rows, missed reminders and late filings logged with root cause, the calendar correction made and the disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of Compliance signs off the annual calendar baseline and every correction made after a missed or unowned obligation

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every calendar row for the period — obligation x writing company x jurisdiction — plus the independently derived list of obligations that should exist for the licensed footprint

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of derived obligations present on the calendar with a named owner; 100% of due rows closed with a retained confirmation; any missing row, unowned row, or filing closed without evidence is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous; completeness of the calendar is tested quarterly and the full baseline-to-state-checklist rebuild is tested annually

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not maintain the calendar or hold a submitter role on any tested obligation

Evidence location for test results.value: Filing calendar completeness test workpaper (derived obligation list, calendar comparison, timeliness evidence trace, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository by quarter

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Calendar extract by jurisdiction showing obligation, due date, filing date and confirmation reference, producible to the Alaska Division of Insurance within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Reporting Manager answers filing-history questions from the calendar and confirmation register; the Head of Compliance clears any statement to a state about a missed obligation

checklist.step: Establish the licensed footprint the calendar must cover
actions: Pull the current certificate of authority status for every writing company from the state licensing records and the NAIC company demographics.
Build the company-by-jurisdiction matrix covering all 51 jurisdictions, marking licensed, accredited surplus lines eligible, or not licensed.
Reconcile the matrix to the licensed-state list shown on each company's Jurat page and resolve any difference before the calendar is built.
Have the Compliance Officer confirm any state where the company is writing but the licence status is unclear.
checklist.done: a reconciled company-by-jurisdiction licensing matrix covering all 51 jurisdictions exists and agrees to the Jurat lists.

checklist.step: Baseline the calendar from each jurisdiction's own filing checklist
actions: Obtain each state's current annual and quarterly filing checklist and read the required-filing list for the blank types the group files.
Create one calendar row per obligation per company per jurisdiction, recording obligation name, statutory due date, filing route and whether NAIC distribution satisfies the state.
Attach the dated checklist page used to create each row so the calendar is source-linked rather than carried forward on trust.
Version the baseline with the statement year and have the Head of Compliance approve it before the year opens.
checklist.done: an approved, source-linked calendar baseline exists with one row per obligation per company per jurisdiction.

checklist.step: Add the NAIC-driven obligations that no single state checklist lists
actions: Add rows for the NAIC-level obligations: annual blank March 1, quarterlies May 15 / August 15 / November 15, RBC March 1, Actuarial Opinion March 1, Actuarial Opinion Summary March 15, April 1 supplementals, MCAS April 30, audited report June 1 and the August 1 internal control communication.
Add the holding company filings — the registration statement and any Form D prior-notice transactions — with the domiciliary state's own due dates.
Mark which rows are satisfied by a single NAIC upload distributed to all states and which require a per-jurisdiction action.
Cross-check the NAIC row list against the current NAIC filing requirements summary rather than last year's calendar.
checklist.done: every NAIC-level and holding company obligation is on the calendar with its own due date and distribution treatment.

checklist.step: Assign a named preparer, reviewer and submitter to every calendar row
actions: Set preparer, reviewer and submitter by name — not by team — on every row, and set a named backup for each.
Confirm each named submitter holds the iSite+ or state portal entitlement the row requires, and raise provisioning where they do not.
Reject any row left with a team mailbox as owner, since unowned rows are the mechanism by which filings are missed.
Publish the owner list to the Controller and the Head of Compliance for confirmation.
checklist.done: every calendar row names a preparer, reviewer, submitter and backup, each with the access their role requires.

checklist.step: Configure the reminder and escalation ladder on every row
actions: Set T-30, T-14, T-5 and T-1 reminders against the statutory due date on every row, addressed to the named preparer and copied to the reviewer.
Configure auto-escalation so an unacknowledged T-5 reminder notifies the Regulatory Reporting Manager and an unacknowledged T-1 notifies the Controller the same day.
Set internal target dates three business days ahead of the statutory date so the reminder ladder protects a buffer rather than the deadline itself.
Test the ladder on a sample row at configuration time and keep the test evidence.
checklist.done: every row carries a tested four-stage reminder ladder with escalation to named managers and a three-day internal buffer.

checklist.step: Run the in-year change intake from bulletins and NAIC adoptions
actions: Monitor state insurance department bulletin pages and NAIC Blanks (E) Working Group adoptions on a defined weekly cadence and log each item that touches a filing obligation.
Assess each change for its effect on the calendar — new obligation, changed due date, changed route, withdrawn obligation — and record the assessment on the change log.
Update the affected calendar rows within five business days of the assessment and re-attach the new source document.
Notify the affected preparer and submitter of every changed row directly rather than relying on them noticing.
checklist.done: regulatory changes are logged weekly, assessed, applied to the calendar within five business days and notified to affected owners.

checklist.step: Maintain the licensing-change feed into the calendar
actions: Take new licence approvals, licence surrenders and withdrawals from the Compliance Officer as they occur.
Add the full obligation set for a newly licensed jurisdiction on the day the certificate of authority is issued, including the first partial-year filing.
For withdrawals, keep the obligation rows open until the state confirms the final filing requirement is satisfied — withdrawal does not end the obligation on the day of surrender.
Record the licensing event reference on every row it created or closed.
checklist.done: every licensing change is reflected on the calendar the same week, with withdrawal rows kept open until the state's final filing is satisfied.

checklist.step: Work the weekly forward view and clear the at-risk rows
actions: Run the calendar's 30-day forward view every Monday and list every row not yet in preparation.
Contact the named preparer for each at-risk row and record their committed readiness date on the row.
Flag rows dependent on an upstream deliverable — actuarial opinion, audited statements, MCAS data build — and confirm the upstream owner's date.
Escalate any row with no committed date to the Regulatory Reporting Manager the same day.
checklist.done: the 30-day forward view is worked weekly and every at-risk row has a committed readiness date or an escalation.

checklist.step: Capture the timeliness evidence on every filed row
actions: On submission, record on the calendar row the actual filing date and time, the confirmation reference and the file name of the confirmation artefact.
Attach the confirmation PDF — NAIC Financial Data Repository receipt, MCAS attestation receipt, state portal confirmation or courier proof of delivery — to the row.
Compute and store days-early or days-late against the statutory date on the row itself so timeliness is a data field, not a recollection.
Refuse to mark a row Closed without an attached confirmation.
checklist.done: every closed row carries an actual filing timestamp, a confirmation artefact and a computed days-to-deadline value.

checklist.step: Reconcile the calendar to the submission register every month
actions: Compare rows due in the month to the submission register and to the NAIC confirmation log, in both directions.
List rows due but not closed, and submissions made with no matching calendar row — the latter proves the calendar was incomplete.
Resolve every difference within five business days and record the correction made to the calendar.
Sign the monthly reconciliation and issue it to the Head of Compliance and the Controller.
checklist.done: a signed monthly two-way reconciliation exists with every difference resolved and the calendar corrected.

checklist.step: Report timeliness performance to management each quarter
actions: Build the quarterly timeliness dashboard: on-time percentage by jurisdiction, by obligation type and by company, with the count of rows closed after the statutory date.
Show ageing of open calendar rows past their internal target date and the rows escalated during the quarter.
Present to the Compliance Committee with the root cause of every late filing and the corrective action taken.
File the pack in the compliance evidence repository under the quarter.
checklist.done: a quarterly timeliness pack with on-time rates, escalations and root causes has been presented and filed.

checklist.step: Log and correct every missed or unowned obligation
actions: Open an issue the same business day a row passes its statutory date unclosed, or an obligation is found with no calendar row.
Record whether the failure was calendar completeness, ownership, reminder configuration or preparation, since the corrective actions differ.
Correct the calendar immediately — add the row, assign the owner, fix the date — and record the correction reference on the issue.
Have the Head of Compliance sign off the correction and any notification made to the affected state.
checklist.done: every miss has a same-day issue, a root cause category, an applied calendar correction and Head of Compliance sign-off.

checklist.step: Rebuild and re-baseline the calendar for the next statement year
actions: Rebuild the calendar for the coming year from the states' newly published checklists rather than by rolling the prior-year calendar forward.
Produce a difference report between the rolled-forward and the rebuilt versions and investigate every difference.
Have the Head of Compliance approve the new baseline before January 1 so the March 1 cycle runs on approved rows.
Archive the closing year's calendar as a locked version.
checklist.done: the next year's calendar is rebuilt from state sources, differenced against the roll-forward, approved before January 1 and the prior year locked.

checklist.step: Prove business continuity of the calendar and its owners
actions: Confirm every calendar row's backup owner can perform the filing, including holding the required iSite+ or state portal entitlement.
Run a table-top test covering a March 1 cycle with the primary submitter unavailable and record how the backup completed the submission.
Confirm the calendar and confirmation evidence are recoverable within the agreed recovery time objective from the repository backup.
Record the test result and any gap with an owner and a date.
checklist.done: a documented continuity test shows backup owners can file on time with the access and evidence they need.

checklist.step: Archive calendar versions and timeliness evidence for retention
actions: File each approved calendar baseline version, the change log, the monthly reconciliations, the quarterly packs and all confirmation artefacts under the statement year.
Apply the 7-year retention label and lock the closed-year folder against edit.
Confirm retrieval by jurisdiction, company code, obligation and due date works from the index.
Confirm closure to the Regulatory Reporting Manager and the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: calendar versions, reconciliations and confirmations are archived, locked, retention-labelled and retrievable by jurisdiction and obligation.

testing.step: Derive the obligation population independently of the calendar
actions: Take the licensed company-by-jurisdiction matrix from state licensing records and the NAIC company demographics.
For each licensed jurisdiction, read that state's current filing checklist and list the obligations it imposes for the blank types filed.
Add the NAIC-level obligations and the holding company filings from the current NAIC and domiciliary requirements.
Sign the derived population as complete and record every source document and its date.
testing.done: an independently derived obligation population exists, sourced from state checklists and NAIC requirements, and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the derived population to the filing calendar in both directions
actions: Match each derived obligation to a calendar row on company, jurisdiction, obligation and due date.
List derived obligations with no calendar row — these are completeness failures and are the most serious finding available here.
List calendar rows with no derived obligation and confirm each is a genuine extra rather than a stale row from a surrendered licence.
Confirm the due date on every matched row equals the statutory date in the source checklist, not an internal target.
testing.done: the calendar reconciles to the derived population in both directions, with every missing or stale row listed.

testing.step: Draw and document the calendar row sample
actions: Take 100% of rows for the domiciliary jurisdiction and 100% of rows for obligations with a statutory penalty for lateness.
Select 30 further rows at random across jurisdictions and obligation types using a recorded seed.
Force inclusion of every row added or amended in-year by the change intake process.
Record population size, seed, selection date and selector so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering domiciliary rows, penalty-bearing obligations and all in-year changes is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the due-date determination against the state source
actions: For each sampled row, open the jurisdiction's current filing checklist or statute and determine the due date yourself before reading the calendar row.
Compare your determination to the row's recorded due date and to the attached source capture.
Treat a correct date supported by a stale or missing source capture as an exception, since the control is the sourcing, not the memory.
Capture the dated source page into the workpaper for every sampled row.
testing.done: each sampled row has an independently determined due date and a dated source capture in the workpaper.

testing.step: Test ownership and access on the sampled rows
actions: Confirm each sampled row names a preparer, reviewer, submitter and backup as individuals rather than teams or mailboxes.
Confirm the named submitter and backup held the iSite+ or state portal entitlement needed on the row's due date, using the access records.
Confirm named owners were employed and in role on the due date using the HR record.
Flag rows whose owner has since left with no reassignment.
testing.done: every sampled row has individually named, in-role owners who held the required filing access on the due date.

testing.step: Test the reminder ladder and the escalation record
actions: For each sampled row, retrieve the reminder log and confirm the T-30, T-14, T-5 and T-1 notifications were generated and delivered.
Confirm each reminder was acknowledged by the named recipient, and where it was not, that the auto-escalation to the Regulatory Reporting Manager or Controller actually fired.
Compare the escalation log to the rows that were subsequently late — a late row with no escalation is a control failure on top of the late filing.
Capture the reminder and escalation records into the workpaper.
testing.done: reminder generation, acknowledgement and escalation are evidenced for every sampled row, with unescalated late rows identified.

testing.step: Trace closed rows to retained timeliness evidence
actions: For each sampled closed row, open the attached confirmation artefact and confirm it names the right company, jurisdiction, obligation and period.
Compare the confirmation's acceptance timestamp to the filing date recorded on the row and to the statutory due date.
Recompute the days-early or days-late value stored on the row and correct any row where the stored value is wrong.
Treat any row marked Closed with no retrievable confirmation as an unevidenced filing.
testing.done: every sampled closed row has a matching confirmation artefact and an independently recomputed timeliness value.

testing.step: Test the in-year change intake and the licensing feed
actions: Take an independent list of bulletins and NAIC adoptions issued in the period that touch filing obligations, from the state bulletin pages directly.
Confirm each appears on the change log with an assessment and, where relevant, a calendar row updated within five business days.
Take the period's licence approvals and surrenders from the Compliance Officer and confirm the calendar gained or retired the correct rows on the right dates.
Flag any change assessed but not applied, and any licence event with no calendar effect.
testing.done: independently sourced regulatory and licensing changes are all traced to assessed, timely calendar updates.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the company, jurisdiction, obligation, due date and the specific failure.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list — obligation missing from calendar, stale row, wrong due date, unowned row, reminder not fired, no escalation, unevidenced closure — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and confirm the calendar correction has actually been applied, referencing the corrected row.
Carry every open issue into the next quarterly completeness test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a referenced calendar correction.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute calendar completeness percentage, ownership completeness percentage and on-time percentage against the 100% thresholds.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, citing the workpaper references behind each measure.
Have the reviewer, who neither maintains the calendar nor submits any tested obligation, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper stating completeness, ownership and on-time percentages with a conclusion and committee date is filed.
