Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the NAIC Market Regulation Handbook standards for claims, underwriting, complaint handling, marketing and producer licensing, read against each state's unfair claims settlement practices and unfair trade practices statutes (rep: Alaska Statutes Title 21; also Alabama Title 27 and the Arkansas Insurance Code)

In-scope processes.value: The conduct areas MCAS reports on and a market conduct exam tests: claims handling and settlement timeliness, underwriting and rating decisions, cancellations and non-renewals, complaint handling and response, replacement and suitability, and producer appointment and termination

In-scope systems.value: Controlled procedure library holding the approved, versioned conduct procedures, linked to the claims, policy administration and complaint systems in which the procedures are executed

Compliance procedure documented.value: Market Conduct Procedure Governance Standard — procedure inventory by conduct area and state variation, drafting and citation rules, annual review cycle, approval authority, publication and training

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with the owning business head; each procedure re-approved at least annually and on any statutory, bulletin or MCAS definition change

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual review of every conduct procedure completed before the April 30 MCAS attestation, so the attesting officer is signing against current procedures; state bulletin changes applied within 30 days of publication

Deadline reminders configured.value: Each procedure carries a review-due date with reminders at T-60 and T-30 days, and an overdue procedure escalates to the Head of Compliance and the owning business head

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Every approved procedure version, its approval record, the citation map, the training completion record and the review evidence retained 7 years so an exam can see the procedure as it stood on any past date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Overdue reviews, unapproved procedures in use, and procedures found contradicted by actual practice logged as compliance exceptions with owner and disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of Compliance signs off every out-of-cycle procedure change and any remediation arising from a procedure-versus-practice gap

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every conduct procedure in the inventory across the MCAS lines and the 51 jurisdictions, plus the state-specific variation addenda and the training records attached to each

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of conduct areas covered by a current, approved procedure; zero procedures past their review date; zero procedures whose stated standard conflicts with the statutory standard or with the observed practice in a sampled file

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is an annual review with continuous change intake; the test runs annually before the MCAS attestation and on any exam notice

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not own or have drafted any sampled procedure and must sit outside the owning business unit

Evidence location for test results.value: Conduct procedure test workpaper (inventory coverage map, version and approval trace, procedure-to-practice comparison, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Procedure set with version history, approval records and citation map, producible to an Alaska Division of Insurance market conduct examiner within 5 business days of an exam call letter

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager coordinates the exam response and the procedure production; Regulatory Counsel clears any written position on a conduct standard before it goes to the examiner

checklist.step: Map the conduct areas that MCAS and a market conduct exam will reach
actions: List the MCAS lines the group files — private passenger auto, homeowners, life, annuity, long-term care, health and any others meeting the premium threshold.

For each line, list the conduct areas the MCAS data elements and the NAIC Market Regulation Handbook chapters reach: claims handling, underwriting and rating, cancellation and non-renewal, complaint handling, marketing and sales, producer licensing and appointment.
Record for each conduct area the business unit that performs it and the system of record in which it is executed.
Publish the map as the scope statement for the procedure inventory and have the Head of Compliance approve it.
checklist.done: an approved scope map links every MCAS line to its conduct areas, owning business unit and system of record.

checklist.step: Build the procedure inventory against that map and find the gaps
actions: List every existing written procedure covering a mapped conduct area with its document number, version, approval date and review-due date.
Mark each conduct area covered, partially covered or uncovered, and name the missing document for every gap.
Identify procedures that exist only as desk notes, intranet pages or training decks — these are not controlled procedures and must be raised as gaps.
Issue the gap list with an owner and a drafting date for each missing procedure.
checklist.done: the inventory shows coverage status for every mapped conduct area and each gap has a named owner and drafting date.

checklist.step: Write the claims handling procedures to the statutory standards
actions: Write the claims procedure covering acknowledgement of notice, contact with the claimant, investigation steps, coverage decision, payment and denial — with the day counts each state's unfair claims settlement practices act imposes.
State where each day count is configured in the claims system as a diary or task so the procedure and the system agree rather than diverge.
Include the denial letter requirements: the policy provision relied on, the factual basis, and the state's required appeal or department-contact language.
Cross-reference the MCAS claims data definitions so claims closed with and without payment, and days-to-settle, are counted the way the MCAS blank defines them.
checklist.done: claims procedures state statutory day counts, tie to system diaries, and use MCAS-consistent claim status definitions.

checklist.step: Write the underwriting, cancellation and non-renewal procedures
actions: Write the underwriting procedure covering acceptable risk criteria, rating and tier assignment, use of credit-based insurance scores where the state permits it, and the adverse action notice requirements.

Write the cancellation and non-renewal procedure recording, per state, the permitted reasons, the notice days required for mid-term cancellation and for non-renewal, and the proof-of-mailing standard.
State how the notice day counts are enforced in the policy administration system and who checks them.
Align the definitions of declination, cancellation and non-renewal to the MCAS underwriting data definitions so the reported counts match the procedure's vocabulary.
checklist.done: underwriting and termination procedures carry per-state reasons, notice day counts and MCAS-consistent definitions.

checklist.step: Write the complaint handling procedure to the department-complaint standard
actions: Write the procedure covering intake of both consumer and department-of-insurance complaints, the required acknowledgement, the investigation, and the substantive response.
Record each state's response deadline for a department complaint — commonly between 10 and 21 calendar days from the department's request — and require the shortest applicable to be diarised.
Define the complaint register fields the NAIC Market Regulation Handbook expects: date received, source, line, reason code, disposition, disposition date and the file location.
Require every department complaint to be logged in the register even when it arrives by phone or is resolved on first contact.
checklist.done: the complaint procedure sets state response deadlines, register fields and mandatory logging of department complaints.

checklist.step: Write the marketing, suitability and replacement procedures
actions: Write the advertising review procedure covering pre-use review, retention of the advertising file, and the state filing requirements for advertising where they exist.

Write the annuity suitability procedure to the state's adopted version of the NAIC Suitability in Annuity Transactions Model, covering the consumer profile information collected, the best-interest basis for the recommendation and supervisory review.
Write the replacement procedure covering the required notices, the notification to the existing insurer and the retention of the replacement register.
Record which states have adopted which model version, since the suitability standard differs materially by state and by adoption date.
checklist.done: advertising, suitability and replacement procedures state the per-state model adoption and the records each requires.

checklist.step: Write the producer appointment, termination and licensing procedure
actions: Write the procedure covering appointment before or within the state's permitted days of the first application submitted, using NIPR Gateway appointment transactions.
State the licence and appointment verification performed before a producer's business is accepted, and the system control that blocks an unappointed producer's submission.
Cover terminations: the NIPR termination transaction, the state's notice-to-producer requirement, and the reporting of terminations for cause within the state's required days.
Cover the annual appointment renewal cycle per state and who reconciles the appointment list to the active producer list.
checklist.done: the producer procedure covers appointment timing, verification blocking, for-cause termination reporting and renewal reconciliation.

checklist.step: Attach a state-variation addendum to every procedure
actions: Build, per procedure, a state variation table listing each of the 51 jurisdictions with the local requirement that differs from the base standard — day counts, notice periods, prohibited practices, required language.
Cite the statute, regulation or bulletin behind every variation row with its effective date.
Where a state imposes no variation, mark it explicitly as 'base standard applies' rather than leaving the cell blank.
Have Regulatory Counsel review the variation table for the states with the most divergent standards before publication.
checklist.done: every procedure carries a complete 51-jurisdiction variation table with cited, dated sources and no blank cells.

checklist.step: Approve, version and publish each procedure through document control
actions: Review and approve each procedure jointly with the owning business head, recording both approvals in the document control record.
Assign a document number, version number, effective date and next review date, and supersede the prior version so only one current version is retrievable.
Publish the current version to the performing teams and remove superseded copies from team sites and shared drives.
Retain every superseded version so the procedure that governed a past claim or policy decision can be produced to an examiner.
checklist.done: each procedure is dually approved, versioned with an effective and review date, published, and its superseded versions retained.

checklist.step: Train the performing staff and record completion
actions: Assign the procedure training to every named role that performs the conduct area, using the HR role mapping rather than a volunteer list.
Include the state variations relevant to each team's book and test comprehension of the day counts and notice requirements.
Set a completion deadline of 30 days from the procedure's effective date and chase non-completions weekly.
Report completion percentage by team to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager and escalate teams below 95%.
checklist.done: training is assigned by role, completed within 30 days of the effective date, and completion is reported with escalations below 95%.

checklist.step: Run the annual review of every procedure before the MCAS attestation
actions: Schedule every procedure's annual review to complete before the April 30 MCAS attestation so the attesting officer signs against current documents.
Require the owner to confirm, in writing on the review record, that the procedure still matches the statutory standard, the system configuration and the actual practice.
Reject a review that changes only the review date — require evidence that the citations and variations were re-checked.
Escalate any procedure past its review date to the Head of Compliance and the owning business head.
checklist.done: every procedure has a completed annual review evidencing re-checked citations, system alignment and practice, before April 30.

checklist.step: Apply statutory and bulletin changes within 30 days
actions: Monitor state bulletins, adopted regulations and NAIC model changes touching the conduct areas on a weekly cadence and log each item.
Assess the effect on each affected procedure and its variation table, and record the assessment with the citation.
Have the owner update, re-approve and republish the affected procedure within 30 days of publication, with training reassigned where behaviour changes.
Record the applied change reference on the procedure's version history so the change trail is provable.
checklist.done: conduct-related regulatory changes are logged weekly, assessed, and applied to procedures and training within 30 days.

checklist.step: Test procedure against practice on live files each quarter
actions: Draw a small quarterly sample of claim, underwriting, complaint and producer files across states and read them against the current procedure.
Record where practice differs from the procedure and determine which one is wrong — the procedure may be stale or the practice may be non-compliant.
Raise a procedure change or a practice remediation accordingly, with the owner and date, and never close the difference by silently rewriting the procedure to match a non-compliant practice.
Report the results to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager each quarter.
checklist.done: quarterly procedure-versus-practice testing is documented with each difference resolved as a procedure or a practice fix.

checklist.step: Hold the exam-ready production pack for the conduct areas
actions: Assemble the standing pack a market conduct exam call letter asks for: current procedures by conduct area, version history, approval records, organisation charts, complaint register and producer appointment listings.
Index the pack so any procedure can be produced as it stood at a stated past date, which is what an exam period actually requires.
Refresh the pack quarterly and after every procedure republication.
Rehearse a 5-business-day production against a mock call letter and record the elapsed time.
checklist.done: an indexed exam pack exists that can produce point-in-time procedure versions within a rehearsed 5-business-day turnaround.

checklist.step: Archive procedure versions and approval evidence for retention
actions: Archive every approved and superseded procedure version with its approval record, citation map, variation table and training completion report.
Apply the 7-year retention label so the version governing any past exam period remains retrievable.
Confirm retrieval by conduct area, state, version and effective-date range works from the index.
Confirm the archive is complete against the procedure inventory and notify the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: all procedure versions and their approval and training evidence are archived, retention-labelled and retrievable by date range.

testing.step: Build the conduct-area population the procedures must cover
actions: Derive the conduct areas independently from the current NAIC Market Regulation Handbook chapters and the MCAS data element definitions for the lines filed.
Add each state's unfair claims settlement practices and unfair trade practices requirements for the licensed jurisdictions.
Compare the derived list to the approved scope map and challenge every area the map omits.
Sign the population as complete and record the Handbook and MCAS definition versions used.
testing.done: an independently derived conduct-area population exists and every omission from the scope map is challenged.

testing.step: Reconcile the derived conduct areas to the procedure inventory
actions: Match each derived conduct area to a current, approved procedure in the controlled repository.
List areas with no procedure, with a procedure only in draft, or covered solely by desk notes or training material.
Confirm each matched procedure's status is Current and that no superseded version is still retrievable as current.
Record the coverage percentage and the specific gaps in the workpaper.
testing.done: every conduct area is matched to a current controlled procedure or listed as a coverage gap.

testing.step: Draw and document the procedure and file sample
actions: Take 100% of procedures covering claims settlement timeliness, cancellation and non-renewal notice, complaint response and annuity suitability.
Select eight further procedures at random from the inventory using a recorded seed.
For each sampled procedure select 10 live files executed under it, spread across at least five states including the domiciliary state.
Record population size, seed, selection date and selector so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample of high-risk and random procedures with 10 live files each across five or more states is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the statutory standard check on each sampled procedure
actions: For each sampled procedure, read the governing statute, regulation or bulletin for three selected states directly before reading the procedure.
State the required standard yourself — the acknowledgement days, the notice days, the response deadline, the suitability standard — then compare to the procedure and its variation table.
Treat any procedure stating a standard weaker than the statute as a failure, and any correct standard with a wrong or missing citation as an exception.
Capture the statutory text relied on, with its effective date, into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled procedure has an independent statutory comparison for three states with the source text captured.

testing.step: Trace approval, versioning and effective dates
actions: For each sampled procedure, retrieve the approval record and confirm both the Head of Compliance and the owning business head approved the current version.
Confirm the effective date, the version number and the next review date are populated and that the review date has not passed.
Confirm the superseded versions are retained and that the repository can produce the version in force on a stated past date.
Flag any procedure in use whose current version was never formally approved.
testing.done: every sampled procedure has dual approval, complete version metadata, an unexpired review date and retrievable point-in-time versions.

testing.step: Compare the procedure to what the sampled files actually show
actions: Read each sampled claim file for the acknowledgement date, contact date, coverage decision date and payment or denial date, and compute the elapsed days.
Compare the elapsed days to the day count the procedure and the state statute require, and to the diary configuration in the claims system.
For sampled underwriting and complaint files, compare the notice content and the response elapsed days to the procedure requirement.
Record each difference and classify it as a stale procedure or a non-compliant practice — the two carry different remediation.
testing.done: each sampled file is compared to the procedure and the statute, with every difference classified as procedure or practice failure.

testing.step: Test the state variation tables for completeness and currency
actions: For each sampled procedure, count the variation table rows and confirm all 51 jurisdictions are present with no blank cells.
Select five states and verify the cited statute or bulletin exists, is current, and says what the row claims.
Confirm any state that changed its standard in the period has an updated row with the new citation and effective date.
Flag rows citing a superseded bulletin or a repealed provision.
testing.done: variation tables are complete for all 51 jurisdictions with five states verified to current, correctly cited source text.

testing.step: Test training assignment and completion against the role mapping
actions: Take the HR role listing for each conduct area and compare it to the training assignment list for the sampled procedures.
Identify performers who were never assigned the training and assigned performers who did not complete it within 30 days of the effective date.
Cross-check whether any performer whose sampled file showed a procedure breach had completed the training.
Record completion percentage by team and flag every team below 95%.
testing.done: training assignment matches the role listing and completion within 30 days is evidenced, with breaches cross-checked to training status.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the conduct area, procedure, state and the specific failure.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list — no procedure, overdue review, weaker-than-statute standard, missing variation row, unapproved version, untrained performer, practice divergence — and an owner.
Set a remediation date, and where a file showed a non-compliant practice, assess whether consumer remediation or a state notification is required with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open issue into the next annual procedure test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a consumer-remediation assessment where practice was non-compliant.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute conduct-area coverage percentage, overdue-review count and procedure-versus-practice exception rate against the stated thresholds.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, citing the workpaper references.
Have the reviewer, who owns and drafted none of the sampled procedures and sits outside the owning business units, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee before the April 30 MCAS attestation and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with coverage, overdue and divergence measures is reported to the Committee before the MCAS attestation.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the MCAS submission; the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager owns the data content and the attesting officer signs the attestation

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the NAIC MCAS Data Call and Definitions for the data year plus each participating state's MCAS bulletin and market conduct statute (rep: Arizona Revised Statutes Title 20; also Title 10 Chapter 5 CCR for California and the Colorado Insurance Code)

In-scope processes.value: MCAS scoping against the $50,000 written premium threshold per state per line, data extraction from claims, policy admin, complaints and producer systems, validation, officer attestation and submission for every state and line blank

In-scope systems.value: The MCAS application in NAIC iSite+ for registration, data upload, validation and attestation; data sourced from the claims, policy administration and complaint systems via the data warehouse

Compliance procedure documented.value: MCAS Submission Procedure — participation scoping, data element mapping to the current data call definitions, extract build and reconciliation, validation clearance, attestation routing and submission

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Regulatory Reporting Manager; re-approved each data year when the NAIC publishes revised MCAS definitions and any new line blank

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: MCAS data for the prior calendar year is due April 30; participation scoping completed by January 31 and the internal data freeze by March 31 so validation and attestation fit before April 30

Deadline reminders configured.value: Milestone reminders at January 31 scoping, February 28 mapping sign-off, March 31 data freeze and T-14 / T-5 / T-1 days to April 30, escalating to the Head of Compliance on any missed milestone

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Scoping premium computation, extract specifications, reconciliations to the source systems, validation clearance, the attestation and the per-state submission receipts retained 7 years in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Missed state-line blanks, failed validations, post-submission data corrections and late attestations logged with cause, corrected submission date and disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of Compliance signs off every MCAS resubmission and every notification to a state that reported data was wrong

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every state-and-line MCAS blank required for the data year, derived from Schedule T premium by state and line against the participation threshold, with the underlying claim, policy and complaint records behind each

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of required state-line blanks submitted and attested by April 30; reported counts must reconcile to the source systems within 0.5%; any missed blank, unattested submission or unreconciled variance above 0.5% is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual for the prior calendar data year; the test runs after the April 30 deadline, with an interim data-quality check at the March 31 freeze

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have built the MCAS extract, cleared validations or attested any blank

Evidence location for test results.value: MCAS submission test workpaper (participation derivation, extract reconciliation, ratio recomputation, attestation trace, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository by data year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per-state MCAS submission receipts, the attestation, the data element mapping and the source reconciliation, producible to the Arizona Department of Insurance and Financial Institutions within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager answers state MCAS data queries and outlier follow-ups; the Head of Compliance clears any resubmission notice sent to a state

checklist.step: Determine MCAS participation state by state and line by line
actions: Take direct written premium by state and by MCAS line for the data year from Schedule T and the state page of the filed annual statement.
Apply the participation threshold in the current data call — $50,000 of direct written premium in the state for the line — and mark each state-line combination in or out of scope.
Check each participating state's own MCAS bulletin for any state-specific threshold or additional line and adjust the scope accordingly.
Issue the scoping matrix by January 31 with the premium figure supporting every in-scope and out-of-scope call.
checklist.done: a January-dated scoping matrix names every in-scope state-line blank with its supporting premium figure.

checklist.step: Register the filing entity and confirm MCAS access in iSite+
actions: Log in to NAIC iSite+ and open the MCAS application for the data year.
Confirm each filing company code is registered for MCAS and that the company contact and attesting officer details are current.
Confirm the named submitter and the attesting officer both hold the MCAS entitlements they need, and raise provisioning at least 15 business days before April 30.
Record the registration confirmation and the entitlement check in the submission register.
checklist.done: every filing company is registered for the data year with current contacts and entitled submitter and attesting officer.

checklist.step: Map every MCAS data element to a source field against the current definitions
actions: Download the NAIC MCAS Data Call and Definitions for the data year and read the change log against last year's version.

Map each data element — claims opened, closed with payment, closed without payment, days-to-final-payment bands, lawsuits opened and closed, complaints, policies in force, new business, cancellations, non-renewals — to a named source field in the claims, policy admin or complaint system.
Record for each element the filter logic: state of risk determination, transaction date basis, and how the calendar-year boundary is applied.
Have the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager sign the mapping by the end of February, before the extract is built.
checklist.done: a signed element-to-source mapping exists for the current-year definitions with filter logic recorded for every element.

checklist.step: Build and freeze the MCAS data extract
actions: Build the extract to the signed mapping, producing one record set per state per line for the calendar data year.
Apply the state-of-risk rule consistently — MCAS is reported by the state where the risk is located, not by mailing address or producer state.
Run the extract at the March 31 freeze, version-stamp it, and store the query and parameters alongside so the numbers are reproducible.
Publish the extract with row counts by state and line to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: a version-stamped, reproducible extract exists per state and line as at the March 31 freeze with the query retained.

checklist.step: Reconcile the extract back to the source systems and the annual statement
actions: Reconcile policies in force and new business counts to the policy administration system's own reporting for the same period and state.
Reconcile claim counts and paid amounts to the claims system's reporting, and reconcile total direct written premium by state to Schedule T.
Investigate and document every variance above 0.5%, and fix the extract rather than annotating the variance where the extract is wrong.
Sign the reconciliation and attach it to the extract version.
checklist.done: the extract reconciles to policy, claims and Schedule T sources within 0.5% with every larger variance documented and resolved.

checklist.step: Run the MCAS data quality edits before uploading anything
actions: Run internal edits mirroring the MCAS validations: claims closed must not exceed claims opened plus opening inventory, days-to-payment bands must sum to claims closed with payment, complaint counts must tie to the complaint register.
Check for structurally impossible values — negative counts, paid amounts with zero claims, in-force counts that fall to zero in an active state.
Compare each element year on year and require an explanation for any movement over 25%, since large unexplained movements draw state follow-up.
Return failing elements to the BI Developer for correction and re-run before the upload.
checklist.done: internal edits, structural checks and year-on-year movement explanations are complete before any upload.

checklist.step: Compile the interrogatory and narrative responses
actions: Answer the MCAS interrogatories for each line, covering matters such as use of third-party administrators, claims systems in use and any mid-year system conversion.
Where a system conversion or a definitional change affects comparability with the prior data year, draft the explanatory comment now rather than answering a state query later.
Have the owning business heads confirm each answer in writing before it is entered.
File the answers and their confirmations with the submission evidence.
checklist.done: every interrogatory is answered with written business confirmation and comparability effects are explained up front.

checklist.step: Upload the data to the MCAS application and clear its validations
actions: In iSite+ open the MCAS application, select the data year, line blank and state, and upload the frozen extract for that state-line combination.
Run the application's validation and read every error and warning returned, recording the code and text.
Fix errors in the extract and re-upload — never key an override into the application to clear a validation.
For each warning left in place, write the explanation the state will read and have the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager approve the wording.
checklist.done: every state-line blank is uploaded with zero unresolved errors and each retained warning carries an approved explanation.

checklist.step: Route the submission for officer attestation
actions: Present the attesting officer with the data summary, the source reconciliation, the year-on-year movement explanations and the validation results before attestation, since attestation is a personal representation of accuracy.
Have the officer execute the attestation in the MCAS application for each state and line, noting that the filing is not made until attestation is complete.
Diarise attestation to complete at least five business days before April 30 so an attestation problem does not become a late filing.
Record the attestation date and the attesting officer name on each state-line row of the submission register.
checklist.done: each state-line blank is attested by the named officer against a reviewed data package at least five business days before April 30.

checklist.step: Submit every state-line blank by April 30 and capture the receipts
actions: Submit each attested state-line blank in the MCAS application and confirm the status changes to Submitted for that state and line.
Download the submission receipt for each and save it named company-state-line-datayear.
Reconcile the submitted list to the January scoping matrix and confirm no in-scope state-line combination is unsubmitted.
Report completion, with the count of blanks submitted, to the Head of Compliance on the day the last blank is filed.
checklist.done: every in-scope state-line blank shows Submitted with a saved receipt and the submitted list reconciles to the scoping matrix.

checklist.step: Handle post-submission corrections through a controlled resubmission
actions: Where an error is found after submission, quantify the affected elements and states and assess whether the reported ratios change materially.
Obtain Head of Compliance approval, then reopen and resubmit the affected state-line blank in the MCAS application, with a fresh attestation.
Notify each affected state that a corrected submission has been made and state what changed.
File the original submission, the corrected submission and the notification together in the evidence set.
checklist.done: corrections are quantified, approved, resubmitted with a fresh attestation, notified to the state and archived alongside the original.

checklist.step: Answer state MCAS follow-up inquiries within their stated deadlines
actions: Log every state inquiry arising from the submission with the state, the data element questioned and the response deadline stated in the request.
Rebuild the questioned element from the frozen extract and the source system before answering, so the answer is reproducible rather than reconstructed.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear any response that concedes a data error or a conduct issue before it is sent.
File the inquiry, the working and the response together against the data year.
checklist.done: every state inquiry is logged, answered from the frozen extract within the stated deadline, and archived with its working.

checklist.step: Feed the reported data into the conduct monitoring baseline
actions: Publish the submitted MCAS figures by state and line into the conduct monitoring dataset so the ratios reported are the ratios monitored.
Compare the reported ratios to the prior data year and highlight the states and lines where the company moved materially.
Hand the comparison to the owning business heads for the conduct metric review that runs quarterly.
Record the handover date so the monitoring cycle and the submission cycle are demonstrably connected.
checklist.done: submitted MCAS figures are published into the monitoring dataset with a year-on-year comparison handed to business owners.

checklist.step: Debrief the cycle and fix the causes before the next data year
actions: Hold a debrief within 30 days of April 30 with the data, compliance and business owners covering every validation failure, reconciliation variance and late milestone.
Record each cause as a data quality, mapping, source system or timeline issue with an owner and a date ahead of the next January scoping.
Update the extract specification and the mapping document with the agreed fixes.
Report the debrief outcome to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: a within-30-days debrief has produced owned, dated fixes to the mapping and extract ahead of the next data year.

checklist.step: Archive the MCAS evidence set for the data year
actions: File the scoping matrix, element mapping, frozen extract and its query, reconciliations, validation results, interrogatory answers, attestations, submission receipts and any corrections under the data year.
Apply the 7-year retention label and lock the folder against edit.
Confirm retrieval by state, line, data year and data element works from the index, since state follow-ups arrive element by element.
Confirm closure to the Regulatory Reporting Manager and the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: the data-year MCAS evidence set is complete, locked, retention-labelled and retrievable by state, line and data element.

testing.step: Derive the required MCAS blanks independently of the scoping matrix
actions: Take direct written premium by state and line for the data year from the filed annual statement Schedule T and state page, not from the compliance team's workbook.
Apply the current data call's participation threshold and each participating state's own bulletin to derive the required state-line blanks.
Compare the derived list to the scoping matrix and challenge every state-line combination the matrix excludes.
Sign the population as complete and record the data call version and premium source used.
testing.done: an independently derived list of required state-line blanks exists and every exclusion in the scoping matrix is challenged.

testing.step: Reconcile submitted blanks to the derived requirement
actions: In the iSite+ MCAS application, list the submissions recorded for the company and data year by state and line.
Match each derived requirement to a submission and list any required blank with no submission.
Confirm each submission shows an executed attestation, since an unattested upload is not a filing.
Record the reconciliation and the NAIC record references in the workpaper.
testing.done: every derived requirement matches an attested submission in iSite+ or is logged as a missing filing.

testing.step: Draw and document the data element sample
actions: Take 100% of the elements the states scrutinise most: claims closed without payment, days-to-final-payment bands, lawsuits opened, complaints and non-renewals.
Select six states at random across the participating list using a recorded seed, forcing inclusion of the representative jurisdiction Arizona and the domiciliary state.
For each sampled state-element pair, select 15 underlying records for file-level tracing.
Record population size, seed, selection date and selector so the sample is reproducible.
testing.done: a reproducible sample of high-scrutiny elements across six states plus Arizona and the domiciliary state is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the element computation from the source systems
actions: Write your own query for each sampled element from the source tables using the NAIC data call definition, without reusing the compliance team's extract query.
Apply the state-of-risk and calendar-year rules from the definition text and compare your count to the submitted figure.
Investigate any difference above 0.5% and identify whether it arises from the filter logic, the state assignment or the date basis.
Capture both queries and both results into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled element is independently recomputed from source with differences above 0.5% explained by a named cause.

testing.step: Trace sampled records to the underlying claim and policy files
actions: For each of the 15 sampled records per state-element pair, open the claim, policy or complaint file and read the dates and disposition.
Confirm a claim counted as closed without payment truly had no indemnity payment, and that a claim in a days-to-payment band actually falls in that band by the definition's date basis.
Confirm the state assigned in the extract equals the state of risk on the policy.
Flag any record whose file contradicts its reported classification.
testing.done: sampled records are traced to files with classification, band and state of risk confirmed against the file itself.

testing.step: Recompute the reported ratios and the year-on-year movements
actions: Recompute the ratios states derive from the submission — claims closed without payment percentage, median days to settle, complaint ratio, lawsuit ratio — for the sampled states.
Compare each to the prior data year and identify movements over 25%.
Confirm every such movement has a retained explanation prepared before submission rather than after a state query.
Record the recomputed ratios and movements in the workpaper.
testing.done: reported ratios are recomputed for sampled states and every movement over 25% has a pre-submission explanation on file.

testing.step: Verify the attestation, its timing and the officer's basis
actions: For each sampled state-line blank, retrieve the attestation record and confirm the attesting officer's name, title and date.
Confirm the attestation pre-dates the April 30 deadline and post-dates the final data upload for that blank.
Confirm the officer was given the data summary, reconciliation and validation results before attesting, by locating the package sent to them.
Flag any attestation executed by someone without the authority recorded in the MCAS registration.
testing.done: every sampled attestation is dated correctly, executed by the registered officer, and supported by a pre-attestation review package.

testing.step: Recompute submission timeliness and test correction handling
actions: Read the submission receipt timestamp for each sampled blank and compute days early or late against April 30.
For any resubmission in the period, confirm Head of Compliance approval, a fresh attestation, a state notification and archived copies of both versions.
Confirm any state follow-up inquiry was answered within the deadline the state stated in its request.
Tabulate timeliness for submissions, resubmissions and inquiry responses.
testing.done: submission, resubmission and inquiry-response timeliness are computed with correction controls verified.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the data year, state, line, element and the specific failure.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list — scoping miss, mapping error, state-of-risk error, date-basis error, validation overridden, late attestation, missing explanation — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where reported data was materially wrong, agree whether a corrected MCAS submission and a state notification are required.
Carry every open issue into next data year's test and into the extract specification as a mandatory fix.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a resubmission decision where reported data was wrong.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute blanks-submitted completeness, element reconciliation variance and on-time percentage against the stated thresholds.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, citing the workpaper references.
Have the reviewer, who built no extract, cleared no validation and attested no blank, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with completeness, variance and timeliness measures, a conclusion and a committee date is filed.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the NAIC MCAS ratio definitions and the Market Regulation Handbook market analysis chapters, read with each state's unfair claims settlement practices standards (rep: Alaska Statutes Title 21; also Alabama Title 27 and the Arkansas Insurance Code)

In-scope processes.value: Quarterly monitoring of the conduct measures states benchmark: claims closed without payment, median and mean days to settle, claims closed beyond the statutory day count, complaint counts and complaint index, lawsuit ratios, cancellation and non-renewal rates, and replacement and suitability rates by state and line

In-scope systems.value: Conduct metrics dashboard built on the claims, policy administration and complaint data in the warehouse, using the same definitions as the MCAS submission

Compliance procedure documented.value: Conduct Metrics Monitoring Procedure — metric definitions matched to MCAS, benchmark sources, threshold setting, quarterly review cadence, outlier investigation and escalation

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with the Chief Claims Officer and the Chief Underwriting Officer; thresholds re-approved annually after each MCAS data year

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Quarterly review completed within 30 days of quarter end; the Q1 review is timed before the April 30 MCAS attestation so outliers are known before they are reported

Deadline reminders configured.value: Dashboard refresh and review-meeting reminders at quarter end plus 10, 20 and 28 days, escalating to the Head of Compliance if the review slips past day 30

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Metrics breaching threshold, missed reviews and overdue outlier actions logged with root cause, owner and disposition, and linked to any consumer remediation

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of Compliance signs off closure of every threshold breach action plan and any decision to accept an out-of-benchmark position

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every metric x state x line published in the quarter's pack, plus the underlying claim, policy and complaint records for the metrics tested and the outlier actions open in the period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Every published metric must reconcile to source within 0.5% and use the MCAS definition; every threshold breach must have an investigation within 30 days and an owned action; an unexplained breach open beyond 90 days is a fail

Evidence location for test results.value: Conduct metrics test workpaper (metric recomputation, benchmark verification, outlier action trace, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository by quarter

checklist.step: Define the monitored metric set to the MCAS definitions
actions: List the metrics to monitor by line: claims closed without payment percentage, median and mean days to final payment, percentage of claims closed beyond the state's statutory day count, complaints per 1,000 policies, lawsuit ratio, cancellation and non-renewal rates, and for life and annuity the replacement and suitability rates.
Write each metric's definition using the current NAIC MCAS data call wording so the monitored number and the reported number are the same number.
Assign a named business owner to each metric — Claims Director for settlement metrics, Underwriting Quality Manager for termination metrics, Complaints Manager for complaint metrics.
Have the Head of Compliance approve the metric set and the definitions before the quarter's dashboard is built.
checklist.done: an approved metric set exists with MCAS-worded definitions and a named business owner per metric.

checklist.step: Source the external benchmarks the states actually use
actions: Obtain the published NAIC MCAS industry ratio ranges for each line and data year and record the ratio, the line and the year on the benchmark sheet.
Obtain the company's complaint index from the NAIC Consumer Information Source and each state's own published complaint data where available.
Record the statutory day counts per state that define 'beyond deadline' for claims, since that benchmark is a statute rather than an industry average.
Date and cite every benchmark so the comparison can be defended, and refresh the sheet when the NAIC publishes new ratios.
checklist.done: a dated, cited benchmark sheet holds industry ratio ranges, complaint index values and statutory day counts by state.

checklist.step: Set the internal thresholds and the escalation tiers
actions: Set, per metric and line, a green, amber and red threshold expressed against the benchmark — for example red where the metric sits outside the industry range or above the statutory day count in any state.
Set a hard red for any state where a metric would place the company in a regulator's outlier band, since that is what triggers market analysis attention.
Define the escalation tier for each colour: amber to the metric owner, red to the business head and the Compliance Committee.
Have the Chief Claims Officer and the Chief Underwriting Officer agree the thresholds before publication, and re-approve them annually.
checklist.done: approved green/amber/red thresholds with escalation tiers exist per metric and line, agreed with the owning business heads.

checklist.step: Build the quarterly metric dataset from the same sources as MCAS
actions: Build the metric queries from the MCAS extract specification so the definitions, state-of-risk rule and date basis are identical.
Produce the metrics by state, by line and by quarter, with the rolling four-quarter view the states' analyses tend to use.
Version-stamp the dataset and retain the queries so any published number can be reproduced later.
Publish row counts and the reconciliation control totals with the dataset.
checklist.done: a version-stamped quarterly metric dataset exists, built on the MCAS specification, with retained queries and control totals.

checklist.step: Reconcile the metric dataset to the source systems
actions: Reconcile claim counts and settlement dates to the claims system's own operational reporting for the same quarter and state.
Reconcile in-force policy counts to the policy administration system and complaint counts to the complaint register.
Document every variance above 0.5% and correct the dataset where the dataset is wrong before anything is published.
Sign the reconciliation and attach it to the dataset version.
checklist.done: the metric dataset reconciles to claims, policy and complaint sources within 0.5% with larger variances resolved.

checklist.step: Publish the quarterly conduct dashboard with benchmark comparison
actions: Publish each metric by state and line with the benchmark value, the variance to benchmark and the RAG colour applied from the approved thresholds.
Show the rolling four-quarter trend and mark each state that moved colour since last quarter.
Include a drill-through from every red cell to the underlying claim, policy or complaint records so an investigation can start from the number.
Restrict edit rights so business owners can read and drill but cannot alter the definitions or thresholds.
checklist.done: the dashboard publishes RAG-coloured metrics by state and line with trend, movement flags and record-level drill-through.

checklist.step: Hold the quarterly conduct metric review within 30 days of quarter end
actions: Convene the review with the Claims Director, the Underwriting Quality Manager, the Complaints Manager and the Head of Compliance within 30 days of quarter end.
Walk every red and newly amber state-metric and require the metric owner to state the cause and the action, not merely acknowledge the number.
Minute the decisions with owner and date for each action and issue the minutes within five business days.
Time the Q1 review to complete before the April 30 MCAS attestation so the attesting officer knows the outliers being reported.
checklist.done: a minuted quarterly review has covered every red and newly amber state-metric with an owned, dated action, and Q1 precedes April 30.

checklist.step: Investigate every red metric down to file level
actions: For each red state-metric, pull 25 underlying files from the dashboard drill-through and read them for the driver — coverage disputes, vendor delays, staffing, a single large event, or a genuine handling failure.
Separate data-driven reds (a definition or coding issue) from conduct-driven reds (files genuinely handled outside the standard), since the remediation differs entirely.
Quantify consumer impact where the driver is conduct — late payments, interest owed, wrongly denied claims.
Write the investigation memo with the file references, the driver and the recommendation within 30 days of the review.
checklist.done: each red state-metric has a 25-file investigation memo naming the driver, distinguishing data from conduct, and quantifying consumer impact.

checklist.step: Open and track corrective action for conduct-driven outliers
actions: Open an action for each conduct-driven red naming the process change — diary configuration, staffing, vendor service level, procedure update, targeted training — with an owner and a date.
Where consumer harm is quantified, agree the remediation with Regulatory Counsel: payment of interest, reopening claims, or a state notification where the statute requires one.
Set the metric recovery expectation — the target value and the quarter by which it should be met — so the action has a testable outcome.
Report progress at the next quarterly review and keep the action open until the metric recovers, not until the change is implemented.
checklist.done: every conduct-driven red has an owned action with a consumer remediation decision and a target metric value and quarter.

checklist.step: Correct data-driven outliers at the definition or coding source
actions: Where the investigation shows a coding or definition cause — claims coded closed-without-payment that were withdrawn, state-of-risk mis-assignment, a date basis mismatch — raise the fix against the source system or the extract specification.
Restate the affected historic metric values and mark the restatement on the dashboard so the trend is not misread.
Assess whether the same defect affected the MCAS submission for the data year and, if so, notify the Regulatory Reporting Manager for a resubmission decision.
Record the fix, the restatement and the MCAS impact assessment on the investigation memo.
checklist.done: data-driven outliers are fixed at source, historic values restated and marked, and any MCAS impact referred for a resubmission decision.

checklist.step: Track the company's complaint index and department complaint volumes
actions: Reconcile the internal complaint register to the department complaints recorded against the company in the NAIC Consumer Information Source for the period.
Investigate any department complaint that has no matching internal register entry — an unlogged department complaint is itself a market conduct finding.
Compute complaints per 1,000 policies in force by state and line and compare to the benchmark and the prior four quarters.
Report states where the complaint index moved above the benchmark to the quarterly review with the reason codes driving it.
checklist.done: the internal register reconciles to department complaint data, unlogged complaints are investigated, and index movements are reported by reason code.

checklist.step: Report conduct metrics and open actions to the Compliance Committee
actions: Present the quarterly pack: RAG position by state and line, movements since last quarter, open investigations, action ageing and any consumer remediation under way.
Name the states where the company would appear as an outlier in a state market analysis, since those are the states most likely to open an inquiry.
Obtain committee decisions on any accepted out-of-benchmark position and minute the acceptance rationale.
File the pack and the minutes in the compliance evidence repository under the quarter.
checklist.done: the committee has received the RAG pack, named outlier states and minuted decisions on any accepted out-of-benchmark position.

checklist.step: Prepare the response position for a state market analysis inquiry
actions: Maintain, for each red state-metric, a standing response pack: the metric definition, the value, the driver, the corrective action and the recovery trend.
Rebuild the number from the retained dataset version whenever a state asks, rather than reconstructing it from a slide.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear any response that concedes a handling deficiency before it is sent to the state.
Log the inquiry, the response and the state's follow-up against the state and metric.
checklist.done: each red state-metric has a standing, reproducible response pack and every inquiry is logged with a counsel-cleared response.

checklist.step: Re-baseline thresholds after each MCAS data year
actions: After the April 30 submission, compare the company's reported ratios to the newly published industry ranges for the data year.
Adjust the amber and red thresholds where the industry position has moved, and record the rationale for each change.
Re-approve the thresholds with the Chief Claims Officer and the Chief Underwriting Officer before the next quarter's pack is built.
Version the threshold sheet so each quarter's RAG can be reproduced against the thresholds in force at the time.
checklist.done: thresholds are re-baselined against the new industry ranges, re-approved and versioned before the next quarterly pack.

checklist.step: Archive the quarterly monitoring evidence
actions: File the quarter's dataset version and queries, benchmark sheet, threshold version, dashboard extract, review minutes, investigation memos and action status under the quarter.
Apply the 7-year retention label and lock the quarter's folder against edit.
Confirm retrieval by state, line, metric and quarter works from the index.
Confirm closure to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: each quarter's monitoring evidence is archived, locked, retention-labelled and retrievable by state, line and metric.

testing.step: Build the population of published metrics for the quarter
actions: Extract every metric x state x line cell published in the quarter's dashboard with its value, benchmark, variance and RAG colour.
Compare the metric list to the approved metric set and list any approved metric not published or any published metric not approved.
Add the open outlier actions carried from prior quarters to the population.
Sign the population as complete and record the dashboard version and extraction date.
testing.done: the published metric population is extracted, compared to the approved metric set, and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the published metrics to the source systems
actions: Take the retained dataset version and control totals and compare claim, policy and complaint counts to the claims, policy administration and complaint registers for the same quarter and state.
Confirm the reconciliation the Data Quality Analyst signed actually covers the version that was published, not an earlier build.
Investigate any variance above 0.5% and determine whether the published number or the source is wrong.
Record the reconciliation results by state and metric in the workpaper.
testing.done: published metric values reconcile to source within 0.5% against the exact dataset version published.

testing.step: Draw and document the metric and file sample
actions: Take 100% of red cells and 100% of cells that moved colour during the quarter.
Select 15 further state-metric cells at random from the green and amber population using a recorded seed.
For each sampled cell, select 15 underlying records via the dashboard drill-through for file-level testing.
Record population size, seed, selection date and selector so the sample is reproducible.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all red and colour-moving cells plus random green and amber coverage is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the metric computation using the MCAS definition
actions: Read the NAIC MCAS definition for each sampled metric and write your own computation from the source data without reusing the dashboard query.
Apply the state-of-risk rule and the date basis from the definition and compare your value to the published value.
Treat a metric computed on an internal definition that differs from the MCAS wording as an exception even where the number looks reasonable.
Capture both computations and their results into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled metric is independently recomputed to the MCAS definition with differences and definition mismatches logged.

testing.step: Verify the benchmark values and the RAG application
actions: For each sampled cell, verify the benchmark used against the published NAIC industry ratio range, the Consumer Information Source complaint data, or the state statute for day counts.
Confirm the benchmark is the correct line and data year, since a prior-year benchmark quietly flatters or penalises the comparison.
Re-apply the approved threshold sheet in force for the quarter and confirm the RAG colour published is the colour the thresholds produce.
Flag any cell whose colour was manually overridden and check for an approval.
testing.done: benchmarks are verified as the right line and year and every published RAG colour is reproduced from the in-force thresholds.

testing.step: Trace sampled records to files and confirm the metric classification
actions: Open each of the 15 sampled records per cell and read the dates, payment status and disposition.
Confirm claims counted as closed beyond the statutory day count genuinely exceeded that state's statutory period from the correct start date.
Confirm complaint records counted are department complaints or consumer complaints as the metric definition requires, not a mixture.
Flag any record whose file contradicts its metric classification.
testing.done: sampled records are traced to files with dates, disposition and classification confirmed against the file itself.

testing.step: Test the outlier investigations and their corrective actions
actions: For each red cell, confirm an investigation memo exists, was completed within 30 days of the quarterly review, and names the driver with file references.
Confirm each conduct-driven red has an action with an owner, a date, a target metric value and a recovery quarter.
Confirm consumer harm quantified in the memo led to a documented remediation decision cleared by Regulatory Counsel.
Age the open actions and flag any conduct-driven red open beyond 90 days without escalation.
testing.done: every red has a timely investigation, an outcome-based action, a remediation decision, and no unescalated action over 90 days old.

testing.step: Test the review cadence, minutes and committee reporting
actions: Confirm the quarterly review occurred within 30 days of quarter end and that the Q1 review pre-dated the April 30 MCAS attestation.
Read the minutes and confirm every red and newly amber cell was discussed with a named owner and a dated action recorded.
Confirm the Compliance Committee received the pack and that any accepted out-of-benchmark position carries a minuted rationale.
Flag any quarter with no review, undated actions, or an acceptance with no recorded rationale.
testing.done: review timing, coverage of reds, minuted actions and committee reporting are evidenced for the quarter.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the quarter, state, line, metric and the specific failure.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list — definition mismatch, source reconciliation failure, wrong benchmark, RAG override, late review, investigation missing, action without an outcome target — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where a metric misstatement also affected the MCAS submission, refer it to the Regulatory Reporting Manager for a resubmission decision.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and an MCAS impact referral where the submission was affected.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the metric reconciliation variance, the count of unexplained reds and the ageing of open outlier actions against the stated thresholds.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, citing the workpaper references behind each measure.
Have the reviewer, who owns no monitored metric and sits outside the tested business units, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with variance, unexplained-red count, action ageing, a conclusion and a committee date is filed.
